read:generation.summary:
OpenMAIC's generator is a clean, model-agnostic package wrapped in a heavy, store-tangled app. The package is packages/@openmaic/generation: about 6k lines of TypeScript plus 5.2k lines of Markdown prompts. Its only seam to a model is `AICallFn(system, user, images?) => Promise<string>` (pipeline-types.ts:60-64). It has no provider code, no app imports and none of the OAuth adapter; the OAuth code lives only in the app at lib/ai/providers.ts:57 and :2647-2692. Generation runs in three stages.

1. **Outline:** requirement goes to `{languageDirective, courseTitle, outlines: SceneOutline[]}` (outline-generator.ts:120-186). The app streams this over SSE with an incremental object parser, 2 retries on the same model and one fallback model (app/api/generate/scene-outlines-stream/route.ts:125-186 and :498-812).
2. **Content per scene:** a PPT canvas for slides, quiz JSON, or a whole HTML+JS iframe document for interactive widgets (scene-generator.ts:228-315).
3. **Actions per scene:** one interleaved JSON array of `{type:'text',content}` and `{type:'action',name,params}`, parsed into `Action[]` such as speech, spotlight, laser, widget_* and discussion (scene-generator.ts:1705-1858, action-parser.ts:41-162). Those are assembled into a DSL Scene (scene-builder.ts:22-115).

The browser drives it scene by scene (lib/hooks/use-scene-generator.ts:719-997). The first scene blocks: content, then actions, then TTS, then the page navigates. Later scenes pipeline: content can run in parallel, while actions and TTS stay serial so `previousSpeeches` carries one page's ending into the next. `withGenerationRetry` (5 retries with jittered backoff) runs on top of routes that call the model with maxRetries:0.

**What carries the owner's direction:** the action timeline is the same format live and recorded. lib/orchestration/stateless-generate.ts:1-19 streams the identical text/action array for the live classroom. "Live theater that stays replayable" is exactly an ordered list of spoken beats with attention moves, bound to a scene.

**Quality, honestly:**
- **Solid:** the action prompts (one teacher voice, same-session continuity, spotlight before speech, quiz answer-safety rules, speech written for TTS), the retry helper, the DSL contracts and the test coverage (30 package tests, 29 app tests on the routes and hook).
- **Weak:** the pedagogy in the outline prompt is thin and lecture-shaped, e.g. "quiz every 3-5 slides" (requirements-to-outlines/system.md:71-75 and user.md:94).
- **Weak:** validation trusts the model. Action names are not checked. Laser, video and widget targets are not checked. A bad spotlight id silently falls back to the first element.
- **Weak:** quiz keys and widget correctness are model-asserted; only their structure is checked.
- **Weak:** the fallback narration is hard-coded Chinese (scene-generator.ts:1863-2028).

**How it should come into apps/web: take the theater, not the slides.**
1. Wire the tutor first, per the live tutor spec P0-P3. It is blocked on the tutor branch: 5cffe4c exists only on worktree-wf_a6840288-a70-24, and point_at is not yet in tutorTools.
2. Add one recorded form to lib/types.ts: `Scene.script?: Beat[]`, with `Beat = { say, cues?: {spot, word}[], do?: widget command }`. This matches spec §3.5 authored cues (line 802) and the §3.1 `[[spot:id]]` anchors.
3. Live tutor replies go through cueParser into the same Beats. A session is recorded as Beats plus learner events. Replay runs `lib/attention.ts` plus SpeechOut over the Beats.
4. Port `generateSceneActions` as our own `writeScript(scene, ctx)` on our `model('build')`. Use `Output.object` with a Zod schema where the spot field is `z.enum(` this scene's spot ids `)`, so invalid targets cannot be produced, then filter through guardSpots. Carry over the prompt rules, `buildCourseContext` and the `previousSpeeches` threading.
5. For the outline and scene content, keep our `writeCourse` and `gateWritten`; they are stronger, with Zod and code-checked keys. Borrow OpenMAIC's outline fields (keyPoints, teachingObjective) and the first-scene-first pipelining.
6. Copy as-is, with the MIT notice: generation-retry.ts, plus the text of the TTS-readability, quiz answer-safety and observation snippets. Also take the Kaizen delta's TEACHING_DIRECTIVE and its nickname strip (lib/kaizen/client/course-request.ts:94-150).
7. Leave behind: the PPT slide canvas, the HTML widget generators (the one-workspace spec §6/§7 rules out arbitrary generated code), PBL, multi-agent discussion, the generation-preview UI and the OAuth path.

**Our side needs one fix first:** the course route does not run the safety screen on the goal (app/api/ai/course/route.ts). lib/generate.ts:104 posts with plain fetch, so family names are not scrubbed. Both must close before the generator gets any learner request.

components.what: SSE outline stream. Events: languageDirective, courseTitle, outline (one per parsed object), retry, done, error (header at 8-13). The incremental O(n) parser for top-level objects is at 125-186.

components.what: Quiz generation with the option contract: value is a single letter A-Z, label is the content, answer lists letters. Includes normalizeQuizOptions/Answer (974-1042) and findQuizOptionsContractFailure (930-963), with failure codes through onFailure.

components.what: The model writes a complete HTML+JS document for an iframe. Pipeline: extractHtml (1163-1197), a node:vm compile-only syntax check, widget-config JSON extraction, KaTeX injected from the jsdelivr CDN (post-processor:70-74), and a selector inventory for the action prompt. The interactive-observation snippet defines a data-maic-observation state contract.

It runs arbitrary model JavaScript, pulls third-party CDNs (Three.js from unpkg, visualization3d-content/system.md:358), and has no code-checked answers or verified accessibility. The engineering around it (parse5 script scan, attribute sanitising) is careful.

components.what: Stage 3, the teacher's script. One call per scene returns interleaved speech and actions. Slides: spotlight or laser before the matching speech, 5-10 items, discussion only at the end. Quiz: 1-2 meta lines that never preview or hint. components.quality: The prompts are the best part of OpenMAIC and encode real teaching behaviour (slide-actions/system.md:121-170, quiz-actions/system.md:36-52, interactive-actions/system.md:88-112). When parsing fails, the fallback speech is hard-coded Chinese and still returns success.
components.portability: Adapt (core port). components.what: withGenerationRetry: 5 retries by default, 1 s base, 16 s cap, 20% jitter, abort-aware, plus shouldRetryResult and onRetry events. isRetryableGenerationError recognises 408/409/425/429/5xx, nested cause/lastError/errors, timeouts and network-error message patterns (21-157, 177-234).

read:generation.contracts:
MODEL SEAM: `AICallFn = (systemPrompt: string, userPrompt: string, images?: {id,src}[]) => Promise<string>` (packages/@openmaic/generation/src/pipeline-types.ts:60-64). The package never picks a provider; routes build the closure over callLLM, e.g. app/api/generate/scene-content/route.ts:133-178 with maxRetries:0. Ours is one line over apps/web/src/lib/ai/config.ts model('build').

OUTLINE (stage 1 output), outline-generator.ts:126-128 and outline-types.ts:70-107:
`{ languageDirective: string; courseTitle?: string /*<=120 chars*/; outlines: SceneOutline[] }`.
`SceneOutline = { id; type: 'slide'|'quiz'|'interactive'|'pbl'; title; description; keyPoints: string[]; teachingObjective?; estimatedDuration?; order; languageNote?; suggestedImageIds?; mediaGenerations?: {type:'image'|'video', prompt, elementId:'gen_img_xxxxxxxx', aspectRatio?}[]; quizConfig?: {questionCount, difficulty:'easy'|'medium'|'hard', questionTypes}; widgetType?: 'simulation'|'diagram'|'code'|'game'|'visualization3d'|'procedural-skill'; widgetOutline?: {concept, keyVariables, diagramType, nodes, ...}; pblConfig?; interactiveConfig? /*deprecated*/ }`.

SSE wire format (app/api/generate/scene-outlines-stream/route.ts:8-13): `data: {type:'languageDirective',data}` | `{type:'courseTitle',data}` | `{type:'outline',data:SceneOutline,index}` | `{type:'retry',attempt,maxAttempts,fallback?}` (the client must discard collected outlines, generation-preview/page.tsx:567-576) | `{type:'done',outlines,languageDirective,courseTitle?,taskEngineMode}` | `{type:'error',error}`, plus a `:heartbeat` comment every 15 s.

SCENE CONTENT (stage 2), scene-types.ts:16-46:
- Slide `{elements: PPTElement[] /*absolute left/top/width/height on a 1000×562.5 canvas, ids reassigned to `${type}_${nanoid(8)}` at scene-generator.ts:826-830*/, background?, remark?}`.
- Quiz `{questions: QuizQuestion[]}` with `QuizQuestion = {id; type:'single'|'multiple'|'short_answer'; question; options?: {label, value:'A'..'Z'}[]; answer?: string[] /*letters*/; analysis?; commentPrompt?; hasAnswer?; points?}` (dsl/src/stage.ts:191-214).
- Interactive `{html: string /*full HTML document*/; widgetType; widgetConfig?: {type, ...}; scientificModel?}`.
- PBL `{projectV2: PBLProject}`.
- Routes: POST /api/generate/scene-content `{outline, allOutlines, stageId, pdfImages?, imageMapping?, agents?, languageDirective?, requirements?}` → `{success, content, effectiveOutline}`. Failure is a 500 GENERATION_FAILED; the internal failure codes are 'prompt-unavailable' and 'invalid-model-output' (scene-generator.ts:76-80).

ACTION TIMELINE (stage 3). The model emits `[{"type":"action","name":"spotlight","params":{"elementId":"text_ab12cd34"}},{"type":"text","content":"..."}, ...]` (slide-actions/system.md:13-41). action-parser.ts:41-162 turns it into `Action[]`. The DSL union is dsl/src/action.ts:235-256:
- `speech{text, audioId?, voice?, speed?}`
- `spotlight{elementId, dimOpacity?}` and `laser{elementId, color?}`, both fire-and-forget (261)
- `play_video{elementId}`
- `wb_*` ×12
- `discussion{topic, prompt?, agentId?}`, always last
- `widget_highlight{target: css selector, content?}`, `widget_setState{state: Record<string,unknown>, content?}`, `widget_annotation{target, content?}`, `widget_reveal{target, content?}`

Every action has `{id, title?, description?}`. Sync actions block the next one (267-287). Route: POST /api/generate/scene-actions `{outline, allOutlines, content, stageId, agents?, previousSpeeches?, userProfile?, languageDirective?}` → `{success, scene, previousSpeeches: string[]}`. The route builds ctx `{pageIndex, totalPages, allTitles, previousSpeeches}` at app/api/generate/scene-actions/route.ts:143-150, and buildCourseContext renders it (prompt-formatters.ts:9-50).

WHAT A GENERATED CLASSROOM LOOKS LIKE AS DATA:
`Stage {id, name: courseTitle, languageDirective, style:'interactive', videoManifest, generatedAgentConfigs[{id,name,role,persona,avatar,color,priority,voiceConfig?}] | agentIds, interactiveMode?, taskEngineMode?, createdAt, updatedAt}` (dsl/src/stage.ts:141-174; built at lib/server/classroom-generation.ts:447-474).
`Scene[]`, each `{id, outlineId, stageId, type, title, order, content, actions[], createdAt, updatedAt}` (scene-builder.ts:53-111). For example:
- Slide: content `{type:'slide', canvas:{id, viewportSize:1000, viewportRatio:0.5625, theme:{fontName:'Microsoft YaHei',…}, elements:[text/latex/shape/chart/image…], background}}`; actions `[spotlight(text_x), speech, spotlight(chart_y), speech, …, discussion?]`.
- Quiz: content `{type:'quiz', questions:[…answer:['B']…]}`; actions `[speech]`.
- Interactive: content `{type:'interactive', url:'', html:'<!DOCTYPE html>…<script type="application/json" id="widget-config">…</script>…<script type="application/json" data-maic-observation>…', widgetType:'simulation', widgetConfig:{type:'simulation', variables:[{name,min,max,default}]}}`; actions `[speech, widget_highlight('#angle-slider'), widget_setState({angle:30}), speech]`.
Playback consumes `scene.actions` directly with no compile step (lib/playback/engine.ts:1-24).

LIVE PATH, SAME FORMAT: lib/orchestration/stateless-generate.ts:1-19 and 82-115 stream the identical text/action array, giving ParsedAction `{actionId, actionName, params}`.

OUR SIDE TO MAP ONTO:
- apps/web/src/lib/types.ts:66-130: Block, Visual, Widget (12 typed kinds), Slide/Quiz/Interactive/Project scenes, Lesson. The file header (1-2) says it mirrors OpenMAIC. Scenes have no script or actions today; narration reads the on-screen text (components/stage/narration.tsx:27-84).
- Zod schemas and gates: lib/ai/schemas.ts:131-164, lib/ai/build.ts:141-180. The writer streams NDJSON CourseEvent (build.ts:255-320) through app/api/ai/course/route.ts.
- Live-tutor sync contract (docs/plans/2026-10-07-live-tutor-spec.md): inline anchors `[[spot:<id>]]` with `CUE_MARK` and `Cue {id, word, epoch}` (§3.1, lines 618-651); the voice is the clock (`onWordScheduled`, `heardUpTo`, §3.2); attention scheduler timing (§3.3); lesson-narration cues: automatic `v{i}` → `stage.block.<i>.visual.<kind>` and authored `cues?: {seg, spot, word?}[]` (§3.5, lines 801-802); stage spot ids (§6); one model call per turn (§2.5, line 473).
- The tutor's existing point tool: lib/ai/spot-tool.ts:13-29 PointAtInput `{target, say, steps?}`.

PROPOSED BRIDGE. One recorded form, `Scene.script?: Beat[]` with `Beat = { say: string; cues?: {spot: SpotId; word: number}[]; do?: {widget command typed per Widget kind} }`:
- An OpenMAIC spotlight or laser followed by speech becomes a cue at word 0 of that beat.
- widget_setState and widget_highlight become our typed commands.
- A live tutor reply goes through cueParser into the same Beats.
- A session record is Beats plus learner events.
- Replay is lib/attention.ts plus SpeechOut over the Beats.
risks: Hard-coded Chinese narration ships silently. When the model's action output does not parse, generateSceneActions falls back to Chinese speech, e.g. '现在让我们来做一个小测验…' (scene-generator.ts:1863-2028). /api/generate/scene-actions still returns success, so TTS speaks Chinese in an EN or ES lesson. Any port needs a locale-correct, code-built fallback.

LaTeX is silently corrupted in JSON. json-repair.ts:180-185 tries plain JSON.parse first. A model that writes "\frac{1}{2}" or "\times" with one backslash parses successfully as form feed + 'rac' or tab + 'imes' (verified in node), so the LaTeX repair at 198-210 never runs. K–9 math formulas would render wrong with no error. Structured output with Zod avoids it; if JSON repair is ever ported, it needs a test.

Learner data reaches the model in the upstream flow. The nickname and bio go into the outline prompt (outline-generator.ts:89-92; scene-outlines-stream/route.ts:326-329) and into userProfile for slide actions (generation-preview/page.tsx:914-917; scene-generator.ts:1738). Our rule is that learner names never go to a model. The port must not pass UserRequirements.userNickname/userBio or userProfile at all; the Kaizen delta already strips the nickname (course-request.ts:141-150).

Our own generation entry point breaks two house rules today. app/api/ai/course/route.ts never runs screen() on the goal before writeCourse (only the practice and extract routes do). lib/generate.ts:104 posts with plain fetch instead of aiFetch, so family names in the goal are not scrubbed. Wiring the OpenMAIC generator on top would inherit both. Fix this before any tutor-made lesson generation.

Answers are model-asserted, not code-checked. The quiz key is only checked structurally (findQuizOptionsContractFailure, scene-generator.ts:930-963), and HTML widgets judge correctness in their own model-written JS. That violates AGENTS.md rule 8. Only our typed Widget kinds plus widgetProblems/gateWritten/practice check() may decide right or wrong.

Generated HTML widgets are out of policy for 1.0: arbitrary model JavaScript in an iframe, third-party CDNs (KaTeX from jsdelivr in interactive-post-processor.ts:72-74, Three.js from unpkg in visualization3d-content/system.md:358), unknown accessibility, nothing deterministic to check. The one-workspace spec §6 (the model cannot run JavaScript or select arbitrary DOM) and §7 exclude them; plan 2.6 defers them to a 1.1 sandbox.

The tutor could point at the wrong thing, or at an answer. action-parser.ts:113-117 casts any action name without checking. Laser, play_video and widget targets are never validated. A bad spotlight id falls back to elements[0] (scene-generator.ts:1937-1947). This conflicts with the spotlight guards ('never point at an answer', guardSpots). Targets must be constrained at decode time (z.enum of the scene's spot ids), then filtered by guardSpots and checked again when they fire.

The pedagogy in OpenMAIC's prompts is adult and lecture-shaped: 1-2 scenes per minute, a quiz every 3-5 slides, default audience 'general learners', 15-20 minutes (requirements-to-outlines/system.md:79-89, user.md:93-94). It has no K–2 reading load, no show→try→check order and no misconception step. Keep our WRITER rules, gateWritten and the Kaizen TEACHING_DIRECTIVE; borrow only the action-script rules.

Two competing sync formats. OpenMAIC's interleaved text/action items and the live-tutor spec's inline [[spot:id]] anchors (§3.1) would both end up in apps/web unless one recorded Beat form is chosen. Recommendation: store Beats {say, cues[{spot, word}]} and convert both producers into it, so live, recorded and replayed sessions share one attention scheduler.

The latency budget is incompatible with inline generation. An OpenMAIC scene is two sequential model calls plus TTS (the first scene blocks on content → actions → TTS, generation-preview/page.tsx:919-982). The live budget is p50 ≤ 1.6 s from last word to first sound (spec §2.3) with one model call per turn (§2.5). Lesson generation must therefore be a background job; the live tutor's own reply is the theater beat.

The tutor-first order is blocked. Spec §0.4 requires the tutor branch on foundation before Phase 3, but its tip 5cffe4c is contained only in worktree-wf_a6840288-a70-24 (git branch --contains). point_at is not yet in tutorTools, and no screen mounts SpotlightLayer (spec §0.3).

Cost from layered retries. Client withGenerationRetry defaults to 5 retries (generation-retry.ts:21-23) on top of server fallback models and the outline's 2 retries plus 1 fallback; a 500 from an unparseable scene re-rolls the model up to 6 times. Each attempt must go through lib/server/budget.ts meter/spendGate, with a foreground cap of about 2 like OpenMAIC's own FOREGROUND_SCENE_RETRY_OPTIONS.

The headless upstream path loses course context. lib/server/classroom-generation.ts:555-560 calls generateSceneActions without ctx, so buildCourseContext is empty: no page position, greeting rule or previous speech, and pages may greet or close at random. Copying that job shape without passing ctx repeats the bug.

Multi-agent assumptions are spread through the prompts and code: discussion actions, a random student agentId (scene-generator.ts:1950-1965), generateAgentProfiles (classroom-generation.ts:136-186). KaizenEDU has one tutor. Strip them rather than leave a dormant discussion path that could script fake classmates.

Runtime and bundle hazards. prompts/loader.ts uses node:fs and interactive-script-validator.ts uses node:vm, so they are server-only; only src/browser.ts is browser-safe. OpenMAIC targets ai v6 and next 16.3.3; we run ai v7 and next 16.4. The package itself has no SDK dependency, but buildVisionUserContent (prompt-formatters.ts:109-139) emits v6 image parts with mimeType.

The upstream live tutor puts answer keys in the prompt after submission. lib/orchestration/summarizers/state-context.ts:187-203 adds the correct answer and analysis once a quiz is submitted, which breaks the letter of 'the tutor prompt never contains an answer key'. Do not port the chat summarizers; keep our server-rebuilt items (lib/ai/context.ts) and check_answer.

Licence and OAuth. Ported files must keep THU-MAIC's MIT notice (modules/openmaic-classroom/LICENSE). The 'pose as Claude Code' OAuth path is not in the generation package (grep confirms), but it sits in the app's lib/ai/providers.ts:57 and 2647-2692, which every upstream route reaches through callLLM and resolveModel. Never copy a route or lib/ai file wholesale; bind AICallFn to our lib/ai/config.ts model().

read:audio-media-export.summary:
I read the code only and changed no files. In OpenMAIC 1.1.1, "replay" means playing back a written action list: Scene.actions[] (speech, spotlight, laser, whiteboard, widget, discussion), run by PlaybackEngine with TTS clips rendered ahead of time. OpenMAIC does not record a live session as something you can play back. A live discussion is saved only as chat UIMessage snapshots, a whiteboard op log, quiz attempts and a playback cursor (sceneId, actionIndex). The audio for each live line is synthesized, played once and thrown away (lib/hooks/use-discussion-tts.ts:254). Audio is batch-only: whole-text TTS returned as base64, played through an HTMLAudioElement, with no word alignment. The ElevenLabs adapter calls /text-to-speech/{voice}, not /with-timestamps (lib/audio/tts-providers.ts:1245-1291). Speech input is push-to-talk: MediaRecorder sends a whole clip to /api/transcription, and browser recognition runs with continuous=false and interimResults=false. Sync is per action, not per word: a spotlight fires before a whole speech action and clears after 5 s on one shared timer. Live chat pacing uses the text as the clock (StreamBuffer reveals 1 character every 30 ms).

So for the live loop our apps/web/src/lib/voice is ahead: it already has the streaming ElevenLabs WebSocket with alignment, Deepgram, turn-taking and barge-in. Nothing from OpenMAIC's audio layer should replace it.

Worth porting, by adapting rather than importing:
(1) The run-and-record design: the DSL action contract, PlaybackEngine's state machine with generation tokens and snapshots, the pure choreography timing/cursor/timeline, and seek safety. These become a pure lib/theater player that drives our single SpeechOut and the attention scheduler in word-index space.
(2) The runtime session/record design from @openmaic/dsl runtime.ts and @openmaic/storage runtime/types.ts: records ordered by a store-assigned seq, and anchors (sceneId, actionIndex) that may go stale and must be tolerated. This is the right shape for "every tutor session is recorded".
(3) The pure video-export IR (zod schema, diagnostics, injected timing/assets), plus subtitles.ts and split-cue, kept for a later "playback as video".
(4) Two leaf utilities with no dependencies: pcm-wav.ts and audio-duration.ts.
(5) The scene-tts loop and the ElevenLabs adapter, rewritten as our server-side clip renderer for P5 using /with-timestamps.

Leave behind: render-service (needs Chromium and FFmpeg in a container), PPTX export (built on PPTist), the Postgres owner/asset persistence, the narration allocation and adoption code (leftover legacy migration), media-orchestrator (zustand and Dexie), StreamBuffer, AudioPlayer, and the TTS/ASR routes. Those routes reach the Anthropic OAuth branch through model-config.

The recording itself has to be built on our side. It should be a seq-ordered TheaterRecord log. Each tutor line stores display text, word start times, cues {spot, word}, an optional clip ref and heardUpTo. Learner turns are stored as scrubbed text only, never audio. Checker results come from code, and widget changes are stored as semantic commands. Replay plays this log back without any model call. A lesson is then a saved session with the learner's parts removed, which matches the owner's point that lessons are an extension of the tutor.

The biggest decision is the generator. It writes spotlight elementId values that are PPTist canvas ids, and widget_* targets that are CSS selectors. Playback, geometry and export all assume the 1000×562.5 PPTist canvas. To use the generator we must either retarget its action output to our data-spot ids and Block/Widget scenes, or port @openmaic/renderer, which is 5.2k lines.

read:audio-media-export.contracts:
OPENMAIC (what replay consumes)

- Stage and Scene: dsl/src/stage.ts:141-174 and :228-283. A Scene is SceneCore {id, stageId, title, order, actions?: Action[], whiteboards?, multiAgent?} with type tied to content (slide = PPTist canvas, quiz, interactive, pbl).
- Action: dsl/src/action.ts:235-256.
  - Fire-and-forget (:261): spotlight {elementId, dimOpacity = 0.5}, laser {elementId, color}.
  - Blocking (:267-287): speech {text, audioId?: AssetRef, audioInvalidated?, voice?, speed?}, wb_* (canvas coordinates 0-1000 × 0-562), widget_highlight/setState/annotation/reveal {target: CSS selector, sent to the iframe by postMessage}, play_video {elementId}, discussion {topic, prompt?, agentId?}.
  - The generator emits an interleaved JSON array, [{type:'action', name, params} | {type:'text', content}], which becomes Action[] with order kept; each text item becomes a speech action (generation/src/action-parser.ts:27-45).
- Asset seam: dsl/src/storage.ts:86-93. StorageProvider {put(blob, meta) → newly allocated AssetRef, resolve(ref) → url | null, remove}. Refs are allocated, never content hashes, to avoid an existence oracle (:74-85).
- Playback: lib/playback/types.ts.
  - PlaybackSnapshot {sceneIndex, actionIndex, consumedDiscussions[], sceneId?} (:5-10).
  - EngineMode 'idle'|'playing'|'paused'|'live' (:18).
  - Callbacks onSpeechStart(text), onSpeechEnd, onEffectFire({kind:'spotlight'|'laser', targetId}), onProgress(snapshot), onComplete, getPlaybackSpeed (:32-65).
  - Per-action order: onProgress fires BEFORE advancing (engine.ts:603-608), so a restore replays the current speech.
  - A speech action falls back from clip to browser TTS (only if that provider is selected) to the reading timer (:650-675).
  - A seek replays the whiteboard prefix silently (:181-220), allowed only within a reconstructable prefix (action-navigation.ts:62-92).
- Timeline: choreography/timeline.ts.
  - TimelineSegment {action, sceneId, sceneIndex, actionIndex, startMs, durationMs, advancesCursorMs, blocking} (:128-144).
  - ResolveTimelineOptions {playbackSpeed, getAudioDurationMs(speech), getVideoDurationMs, onUnresolvedVideoDuration 'throw'|'cap'|'zero', …} (:71-126).
  - The no-audio estimate is 240 ms per word with a 2 s floor (timing.ts:113-121).
- Recording envelope: dsl/src/runtime.ts.
  - RuntimeSession {id, runtimeDslVersion, kind, stageId, learnerKey, status active|completed|archived, createdAt, updatedAt as ISO} (:203-225).
  - RuntimeRecord {id, sessionId, seq (assigned by the store, the only order), sceneId?, actionIndex?, subAnchor?, createdAt, payload} (:245-267).
  - RuntimeStore.appendRecord(init, {expectedLastSeq?, sessionTransition?}) and listRecords(sessionId, {sceneId?}) (storage/src/runtime/types.ts:196-206).
  - Chat payload is {kind:'chat_message', payloadVersion:1, message: UIMessage, sessionUpdatedAt} (chat-storage-core.ts:23-28).
  - Whiteboard payload is {payloadVersion:1, operationId, operation} (whiteboard/runtime/types.ts:64-68).
- Video IR: video-export/ir.ts:373. VideoTimeline {schema 'openmaic.videoTimeline', version 4, canvas, config {playbackSpeed, ttsEnabled}, totalDurationMs, scenes[{base, visuals, narration[{actionIndex, startMs, durationMs, text, audio {assetId, durationMs, source 'stored'|'estimated', present}}], effects[{descriptorId 'spotlight.v1', startMs, durationMs, elementId, geometry, params, degraded}], videos, markers}], subtitles[{startMs, endMs, text}], assets {entries}, diagnostics}.
- Zip manifest: classroom-zip-types.ts:14-22 and :114-149.

OURS (binding, apps/web)

- SpeechOut: src/lib/voice/types.ts:38-59 today. Spec §3.2 adds speak(source, {signal, kind, band}) returning a SpeechRun (a Promise with an id), onWordScheduled(word, audibleAt, run), heardUpTo(), duck/unduck, and cancel({fadeMs}).
- Word space: display.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean) (spec §3.1, types.ts:117).
- Cue: lib/voice/cues.ts {id, word, epoch}, with markers written as [[spot:id]].
- Epoch: `${pathname}|${item|scene|'talk'}|${messageId}`.
- Attention: 150 ms lead, glide clamp(240 + 0.3·px, 280, 560), dwell 900/1200 ms, at most 5 moves (spec §3.3).
- Spotlight ids: data-spot (src/lib/spotlight.ts:16-20, guardSpots :307).
- Scenes: src/lib/types.ts:124-130 (slide blocks, quiz, interactive Widget, project).
- Transcript: TutorThread {lines: {role, text, at}[]} (planner/types.ts:53-65).
- Clips: voice/<sha256(text|voice|model|speed)[:16]>.{mp3,json} plus a manifest (spec P5).

PROPOSED PORT SHAPE (from OpenMAIC's runtime design and our sync contract)

- TheaterSession {id, profileId, epochBase, surface, courseId?, lessonId?, status, version}.
- TheaterRecord {seq, at, anchor? {sceneId, itemId}, beat}.
- Beat kinds:
  - tutor.say {run, text (display, scrubbed), wordsAtMs: number[] (delta-encoded, relative to run start), cues: {spot, word}[], clip? {assetId, durationMs, mime}, heardUpTo, cut?}
  - learner.turn {via 'voice'|'text', text (scrubbed), confidence?}, never audio
  - check {itemId, verdict} (from code, display-only on replay)
  - stage.scene {sceneId}
  - widget.cmd {spot, kind, state} (idempotent opId)
  - board.card {tool, payload}
  - safety {referral}
- Replay walks the records in seq order and drives SpeechOut with the clip, or with text pacing in typed mode. It feeds the attention scheduler with audibleAt = runStart + wordsAtMs[word] + outputLatency. It must not write any learning record.
risks: The OAuth adapter comes in through the dependency chain. app/api/generate/tts/route.ts and lib/server/agent-runtime/scene-tts.ts import lib/server/model-config/media.ts (:28-34), which imports ./runtime (:21-28), which imports ./resolve-slot (:15), which imports lib/ai/providers.ts. That module holds the Anthropic OAuth branch (:54-57, :2642-2664). Copying a route, model-config, provider-config or anything that imports them ships the forbidden adapter. Port only leaf functions, and add a verify-time grep in apps/web for 'anthropic-oauth|anthropicOAuth|sk-ant-oat|startAnthropicOAuthRefresh'.

Nothing in OpenMAIC records a live session so it can be played back. The audio of each live line is synthesized, played and thrown away (use-discussion-tts.ts:254). Chat is kept as UIMessage snapshots with no timing or cues (chat-storage-core.ts:23-28). The owner's 'recording or replay able experiences' must be built on our side (TheaterRecord log, client-side clip capture, a replay player). Do not plan as if it exists.

Sync granularity does not match. OpenMAIC cues are per action: a spotlight fires before a whole speech action and clears on one shared 5 s timer (action/engine.ts:308-325, choreography/timeline.ts:368-403). Live pacing uses the text as the clock (stream-buffer.ts:208-211). Subtitles are spread by character weight (split-cue.ts:11-16). Porting PlaybackEngine, StreamBuffer or the descriptors unchanged breaks our binding contract: word-index cues, a 150 ms lead, a ring that never remounts, and no dim in voice mode.

The generator targets PPTist. Its spotlight and laser elementId values are PPTist canvas element ids, widget_* targets are CSS selectors sent into iframes (dsl/src/action.ts:31-42, :205-231), and playback, video geometry and PPTX all assume the 1000×562.5 canvas (video-export/ir.ts CANVAS). Using the generator means either (a) retargeting its scene-action prompts and parser to our data-spot ids and Block/Widget scenes, or (b) porting @openmaic/renderer (5.2k lines plus echarts, motion and shiki). That is an architecture decision to escalate, and replay and export depend on it.

Seek needs reconstructable state. OpenMAIC's action-navigation.ts:16-23 blocks seeking past widget beats. Our widgets (components/stage/widgets/*) keep internal React state, so they need controlled state props plus per-beat state snapshots in the recording. Otherwise replay is play-from-start only after the first manipulation.

Honest records. A replay must never write an Attempt, ActivityEvent, TeachingAct or proof. Checks shown in a replay show the code-checked verdict that was recorded, and are never re-run against a model. A lesson made from a session must strip learner turns and answers before it becomes reusable content. OpenMAIC's quiz runtime records are attempt facts. Do not copy that into replay.

Privacy. Never record learner mic audio (one-workspace spec §9.2: raw audio stays out of the learning record). Scrub learner names at record time (setSpotScrub/scrubNames), so recordings and any later model calls on them hold no names. Recorded tutor audio for live replies must use allocated random ids with private access, following OpenMAIC's own existence-oracle argument (dsl/src/storage.ts:74-85). The spec P5 content-addressed clip path is acceptable only for catalogue and fixed lines.

Storage size. Our store is one whole-document localStorage JSON (src/lib/store.ts header). Per-word timings, cues and clip refs for every session will soon exceed the localStorage quota. Keep theater logs in IndexedDB as src/lib/blobs.ts does, delta-encode the word times, put clips in Blob storage with a retention policy, and extend src/lib/export.ts so family export and delete cover recordings.

Vercel functions cannot hold WebSockets, and the live TTS runs browser to ElevenLabs. Recording the tutor's voice therefore means capturing PCM from player.ts in the client, wrapping it as WAV with pcm-wav.ts (or encoding it), and uploading after the turn, against the voice consent rules. The MP4 render-service needs its own Chromium and FFmpeg container and is out of scope for Vercel.

Demo mode must work with no keys. Replay plays stored clips when they exist. Otherwise it uses a Tier A browser voice, or text-only with typed-mode pacing (spec §3.3, §4). It must not fake word precision with estimateSpeechDurationMs (240 ms per word); the one-workspace spec forbids simulated word timing.

Voice defaults conflict. OpenMAIC falls back to a default ElevenLabs voice (route.ts:107-110 → constants.ts:1550 'EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL'), defaults to model eleven_multilingual_v2, and clamps speed to 0.7-1.2. Spec §2.2 requires ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID and ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID_ES with no default, speed 1.0 (0.94 for K–2 on Flash), never below 0.9, and pacing from band pauses.

Library versions differ. OpenMAIC uses ai ^6, next 16.3.3, react 19.2.3, zod ^4.3, zustand and Dexie. We use ai ^7, @ai-sdk/anthropic ^4, next 16.4.0, react 19.3.0, and no zustand or Dexie. Any code that persists or depends on UIMessage shapes or the store will not transfer cleanly; port pure modules only.

I mapped the AI layer of modules/openmaic-classroom (OpenMAIC 1.1.1 plus the Kaizen delta) against apps/web/src/lib/ai. I changed nothing.

**Verdict.** Take the generator (packages/@openmaic/generation plus @openmaic/dsl) almost as-is, behind a server route of our own. Take none of OpenMAIC's model plumbing.

**The generator.** It has one seam: `AICallFn(system, user, images?) => Promise<string>` (generation/src/pipeline-types.ts:60-64). A grep found no `process.env` and no `fetch` anywhere in its src, so it picks no provider, reads no config and makes no network calls. MIT notice: generation/LICENSE. Two node-only pieces: the prompt loader reads its .md templates with `node:fs` (prompts/loader.ts:5-7), and the interactive validator uses `node:vm`. Both run fine server-side. The only change it needs is the learner name: drop `userNickname`/`userBio` (outline-generator.ts:89-92) and never pass `userProfile` (scene-generator.ts:1715,1738, which feeds the slide-actions template). Bind `AICallFn` to `model("build", meter)` from apps/web/src/lib/ai/config.ts, after `screen()`.

**The OAuth adapter can't ride along by accident.** It lives entirely in the app-side plumbing, which we are not porting:
- lib/ai/anthropic-oauth.ts
- the providers.ts branch at lines 53-57, 2648-2665 and 2692-2700
- lib/server/anthropic-oauth-refresh.ts
- instrumentation.ts:65-69 and 135
- four tests
- docs/history/.../native/openmaic.yml, which sets `apiKey: ${ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN}`

One extra problem: client components import providers.ts (components/settings/model-services.tsx, provider-list.tsx, provider-config-panel.tsx and components/scene-renderers/pbl/v2/submission.tsx). That means the "You are Claude Code" text and the claude-code user-agent also ship in the browser bundle.

**Safety.** OpenMAIC has no input safety screen at all. The only safety handling is treating a content-filter finish as a refusal that is not retried (lib/ai/llm.ts:409-417) and a prompt snippet for image generation (generation/snippets/media-safety-guidelines.md).

**Learner data reaching models unscrubbed:**
- **Nickname and bio** go into:
  - the outline prompt (outline-generator.ts:89-92; app/api/generate/scene-outlines-stream/route.ts:326-329)
  - the director and agent prompts (lib/orchestration/director-prompt.ts:61-67; prompt-builder.ts:82-86, which says "Address them by name naturally")
  - the Pi prompts (lib/chat/pi/prompts.ts:209,267)
  - PBL proficiency seeding
- **Chat messages** go verbatim.
- **Uploaded materials** go to the model and to third-party extractors.
- **The requirement text** goes to third-party search vendors.

The Kaizen delta removed the nickname only on the generation path (lib/kaizen/client/course-request.ts:141-150). The classroom chat still sends nickname and bio from `useUserProfileStore` (components/chat/use-chat-sessions.ts:1682,1877,2001).

**Grading and answer keys.**
- A model grades short answers (app/api/quiz-grade/route.ts). If it can't parse the model's reply, it invents a 50% score (lines 96-103).
- The chat prompt prints the correct answers whenever the request says the quiz was submitted. That flag comes from the client (lib/types/chat.ts:362-372 → lib/orchestration/summarizers/state-context.ts:176-207), so anyone can trigger it.

**Access control.**
- Only a shared ACCESS_CODE plus anonymous owner cookies. Without ACCESS_CODE every model route is open (middleware.ts:47-50).
- No per-user rate limit or spend cap on model routes; the only limiter guards access-code attempts.
- The deprecated request path still accepts `x-model`/`x-api-key`/`x-base-url` (lib/server/resolve-model.ts:233-249) unless `policy.allowWorkspaceProviders: false` is set.

**`configs/` is not model config.** It holds slide-editor UI constants with Chinese labels. Model config is openmaic.example.yml, lib/config/model-slots.ts and lib/server/model-config/*.

**Order that matches the owner's direction (tutor first, lessons as its theater):**
1. Keep our `tutorTurn` as the one brain: one model call per turn (spec §2.5), our safety screen, our tools. Don't port the Pi director or the multi-agent chat: up to 1+6 model calls per learner turn (lib/chat/pi/config.ts:5), with client-sent scenes pasted into the system prompt.
2. Add a server route that screens the request first, then runs the generator: outline → content → actions. Skip the agent-profiles step (solo tutor), web search, materials, TTS and media.
3. Gate the output with our checks, convert DSL scenes and actions into our record, and persist them so the theater can replay them.
4. The tutor calls this route as a tool and talks while scenes stream in. In the historical run at maximum reasoning effort, one scene took more than 8 minutes, so generation must run in the background.

**One gap on our side to fix first.** /api/ai/course never runs `screen()` on the course goal: the route (app/api/ai/course/route.ts:29-48) doesn't, and budget.ts:299 screens only the tutor's "talk" job. Any route that wraps the generator must call `screen()` itself.

- SceneOutline {id, type: 'slide'|'quiz'|'interactive'|'pbl', title, description, keyPoints[], teachingObjective?, estimatedDuration?, order, quizConfig?, widgetType/widgetOutline?, pblConfig?, mediaGenerations?} (outline-types.ts:70-…).

- buildCompleteScene(outline, content, actions, stageId, opts) → CompleteScene | null (scene-builder.ts:22-32).
- Retry wrapper: withGenerationRetry(fn, {label, shouldRetryResult, onRetry}), as used at lib/server/classroom-generation.ts:520-535.

DSL THE THEATER WOULD REPLAY (@openmaic/dsl):
- Stage (dsl/src/stage.ts:141), Scene (:278), SceneContent = Slide | Quiz (:221).
- QuizQuestion {id, type: 'single'|'multiple'|'short_answer', question, options?, answer?: string[] e.g. ['A'], analysis?, commentPrompt?, hasAnswer?, points?} (:196-206). Our QuizQuestion is {id, prompt, choices[], answer: number, hint, explain} (apps/web/src/lib/types.ts:119-126). The conversion drops short_answer and requires a hint.
- Action union (dsl/src/action.ts:235-256): spotlight {elementId, dimOpacity?} (:31-35), laser, speech {text, audioId?, voice?} (:47-…), play_video, wb_open/draw_text/shape/chart/latex/table/line/code/edit_code/clear/delete/close, discussion, widget_highlight/set_state/annotation/reveal. elementId refers to canvas element ids. For our spotlight it must map to our data-spot ids (stage.block.<i>.visual.<kind>, per live-tutor spec §3.5), and speech.text to narration segments, which are the voice clock in spec §3.2.

- getModel(ModelConfig {providerId, modelId, apiKey, baseUrl?, proxy?, providerType?, requiresApiKey?, fetchImpl?}) → {model, modelInfo} (lib/ai/providers.ts:2362). The OAuth branch is keyed on apiKey.startsWith('sk-ant-oat') (:2648-2649; anthropic-oauth.ts:49-51).

- callLLM(params, source, retryOptions?, thinking?, {enabled?, serverManaged?}) (lib/ai/llm.ts:342-349).
- StatelessChatRequest {messages, storeState {stage, scenes, outlines?, currentSceneId, mode, quizResults? {sceneId, answers, results[{questionId, correct, status, earned, aiComment?}]}}, elementReference?, interactiveState?, config {agentIds, sessionType, agentConfigs?, piMaxAgentTurns?}, directorState?, userProfile? {nickname, bio}, apiKey, baseUrl?, model?, providerType?, thinking?, webSearch*} (lib/types/chat.ts:340-440).
- GradeRequest {question, userAnswer, points, commentPrompt?, language?} → {score, comment} (app/api/quiz-grade/route.ts:15-26).

OUR SIDE (binding):
- model(role: 'talk'|'build'|'quick', meter?) → LanguageModel | null (apps/web/src/lib/ai/config.ts:57).
- aiMode() (:32).
- screen(text, locale) → {kind: 'ok'} | {kind: 'crisis'|'abuse'|'offLimits', reply} (safety.ts:8,36).
- tutorTurn(body, model) with LIMITS {messages: 40, chars: 2000} (tutor.ts:20,104).
- TutorContext zod (context.ts:32-45). Per the spec it gains input: 'voice'|'text' and spots[].

- Live tutor spec: one model call per turn (§2.5); [[spot:id]] anchors with cueParser (§3.1); voice-as-clock onWordScheduled (§3.2); latency p50 ≤ 1.6 s from the learner's last word to the first audible sound, of which 600 ms is request → first token (§2.3). Lesson generation therefore runs outside the turn, with the tutor narrating progress, and scene speech actions become narration segments with authored cues.
risks: OAuth contamination by copy. Copying lib/ai/providers.ts, or anything that imports it (lib/ai/llm.ts, lib/server/resolve-model.ts, lib/server/model-config/llm.ts, components/settings/*), brings anthropic-oauth.ts along, because the import is static (providers.ts:53-57). The safe boundary is the generator package plus our own AICallFn, never OpenMAIC's callLLM. Add a CI check that fails if apps/web contains 'sk-ant-oat', 'claude-code-20250219', 'oauth-2025-04-20', 'x-app' or the Claude Code system string.

Learner names into prompts through generator fields. UserRequirements.userNickname/userBio (outline-types.ts:24-31) and the userProfile option of generateSceneActions (scene-generator.ts:1715,1738) put a name straight into the outline and slide-actions templates. Build UserRequirements field by field in our wrapper and add a test that a request containing the learner's nickname never reaches AICallFn. The scrubbing happens in the browser (client.ts scrubBody), so a server route that accepts free text must assume it is already scrubbed, and must only accept requests through aiFetch.

No safety screen in OpenMAIC. Every generator call must sit behind screen(). Today /api/ai/course itself skips screen(goal) (route.ts:29-48; budget.ts:299 screens only talk), so the gap would carry straight into a generator route. Model-written scene text and speech also need the same suitable() check source-course.ts uses before children see or hear it.

Answer keys and model grading. Generator quizzes include short_answer (no key), which OpenMAIC grades by model, with a 50% made-up score when the reply can't be parsed (quiz-grade/route.ts:96-103). Its chat also prints 'Correct answer' whenever the client sends quizResults (state-context.ts:176-207), a client-forgeable flag. Our gate must convert or reject short_answer, verify that keys resolve (gateLesson), and keep keys out of any tutor prompt.

Live latency vs generation latency. The historical run at claude-opus-5 effort max recorded more than 8 minutes per scene, about 90 minutes for 11 scenes (docs/history/.../native/openmaic.yml:42-45). A tutor that 'creates more and more' lessons cannot block a turn on the generator: the spec budget is about 1.6 s p50, with about 600 ms to first token. Generation must be backgrounded and streamed per scene, with modest effort on the build role, and the tutor narrating while it works.

Model-written HTML/JS. Generator 'interactive' scenes are raw HTML and scripts, hosted in an iframe with allow-popups (InteractiveIframeHost.tsx:451). Generated code is out of scope for this release (workspace spec §7, plan §2.6). Map interactive outlines onto our vetted Widget kinds at the gate, or drop them.

Prompt and data heritage. Templates teach language inference with Chinese examples (requirements-to-outlines/system.md:26-37); the upstream locale default is zh-CN. The model writes its own languageDirective, which is then injected into every later prompt. Override it with a fixed en/es directive, as the Kaizen delta does (course-request.ts:79-81), and run the bilingual tests on the output.

Multi-agent assumptions. The pipeline generates agent profiles (classroom-generation.ts:436), and many action prompts assume a teacher plus students (DiscussionAction, agents option). We have one tutor. Skip agent profiles, pass a single teacher agent and drop discussion actions in conversion.

SDK version mismatch. OpenMAIC is on ai ^6.0.168 / @ai-sdk/anthropic ^3.0.71 / next 16.3.3 / react 19.2.3; apps/web is on ai ^7.0.130 / @ai-sdk/anthropic ^4.0.74 / next 16.4.0 / react 19.3.0. Anything beyond the generator (callLLM, stream-fn, @ai-sdk/react hooks) would need rewriting. The generator has no 'ai' dependency, which is why it is the clean port.

Bundling. The generator's prompt loader reads .md templates with node:fs relative to import.meta.url (prompts/loader.ts:5-7; pbl/prompts/loader.ts:13-14), and the validator uses node:vm. In Next 16.4 on Vercel the templates must be traced into the function bundle, or every call fails with 'prompt-unavailable'. Server-only import required.

Spend and abuse. OpenMAIC has no per-learner spend cap and only an optional shared ACCESS_CODE (middleware.ts:47-50). Its default Pi chat fans out to as many as 7 model calls per learner turn (lib/chat/pi/config.ts:5). Any ported path must go through our spendGate, meter and limited, and must check spent() between scenes as writeCourse does.

Data egress to third parties if research or materials are ported: web search (Tavily, Brave, Baidu, Bocha, Exa, MiniMax, Doubao, plus a second Claude client at lib/web-search/claude.ts:118-122), PDF extractors (MinerU cloud, AliDocMind) and ASR vendors chosen by the client. Plan §3.1 bars forwarding learner identifiers; keep research on our own knowledge/ fetchers.
License. OpenMAIC is MIT (packages/@openmaic/generation/LICENSE, root LICENSE) and pi-agent-core is MIT (lib/agent/VENDOR.md). Keep the notice with every copied file or package.

read:playback.summary:
What "live theater" means in this code. The word "theater" never appears in OpenMAIC. It is the owner's word (docs/DECISIONS.md:37-38, docs/STATUS.md:5-10) for OpenMAIC's playback classroom, components/edit/PlaybackChromeRoot.tsx, which has two halves.

(1) Recorded lecture. Each Scene carries `actions[]` in the @openmaic/dsl vocabulary: speech, spotlight, laser, wb_*, play_video, widget_*, discussion. A per-scene PlaybackEngine (lib/playback/engine.ts) plays them in order through ActionEngine (lib/action/engine.ts):
- Speech plays narration audio made ahead of time; with no audio it falls back to a reading-time timer.
- Spotlight and laser fire before the sentence and clear themselves after 5 s.
- Whiteboard draws hold the cursor for fixed animation times (lib/choreography/timing.ts).
- A discussion action shows a "Join / Skip" card after 3 s.

(2) Live. The learner types or records, or joins a discussion:
- The engine saves its place, stepping back one sentence (engine.ts:442-470), and enters mode `live`.
- The chat layer POSTs `/api/chat/pi`, the default; `/api/chat` is the older LangGraph path.
- The teacher's reply streams back in the same `[{type:'text'}|{type:'action'}]` JSON vocabulary. The same ActionEngine runs it on the same stage, and a character typewriter (StreamBuffer) sets the pace.
- Text-to-speech runs once per finished segment. `cue_user` hands the turn back to the learner.
- A 15 s soft close, then a narrow auto-resume rule (lib/playback/auto-resume.ts), returns to the lecture.

Lectures can be replayed. Live Q&A is kept only as a chat transcript (components/chat/use-chat-sessions.ts:634-639) and is never re-performed. So the owner's line "every session recorded and replayable" is new work. The good news: the offline generator emits the same Action vocabulary (packages/@openmaic/generation/src/action-parser.ts:41, scene-generator.ts:1705), so recording a live turn as Action[] fits the existing design.

Verdict on quality:
- **Solid and pure, worth copying:** the DSL action contract and the choreography module (timing, cursor, timeline).
- **Sound core, too many globals:** PlaybackEngine, and ActionEngine. ActionEngine works but is welded to the PPTist slide canvas and its stores.
- **Tangled god-components:** PlaybackChromeRoot (2086 lines, about 30 useState), use-chat-sessions (2249), Roundtable (2201).
- **Unusable against our live-tutor spec:**
  - The Pi director's prompt calls itself a "PoC", has Chinese-only closing phrases, and makes 2-3 or more serial model calls per learner turn.
  - Text-to-speech synthesizes a whole finished segment at a time, without streaming.
  - Voice input is record-then-upload: no streaming, no barge-in.
  - Spotlight dims the screen; the laser defaults to red and remounts on every move.
  - Cue timing is per action, not per word, so it misses the spec's word clock, latency budget and one-model-call rule (spec §2.3, §2.5, §3.2-3.4).

Recommended port, in line with the owner's "tutor first":
1. The live tutor stays ours: `lib/ai/tutor.ts` (one streamText call, safety screen first, deterministic tools) plus the spec's anchors and attention scheduler.
2. Build a small theater layer in apps/web:
   - (a) A trimmed copy of the DSL Action contract. Targets become `data-spot` ids, `wb_*` becomes BoardCard and show_visual, `widget_*` becomes our widgets.
   - (b) Copy lib/choreography (timing, cursor, timeline) and the playback helpers auto-resume.ts and action-navigation.ts, keeping the MIT notice.
   - (c) Rewrite PlaybackEngine at about 200 lines. Inject our SpeechOut (with `onWordScheduled`) and the attention scheduler. No zustand stores, no speechSynthesis in the engine, multi-scene seek.
   - (d) Record each live tutor reply as a "take" (actions plus word times from player.ts) in our store, replayable through the same engine.
3. Later, map OpenMAIC generator output into the same Action list and gate it with our lesson gates.

Leave out the Pi and LangGraph directors, the roundtable, ChatArea and use-chat-sessions, StreamBuffer, discussion text-to-speech, AudioPlayer, the audio recorder, the PPTist whiteboard and overlays, and everything under lib/ai/providers.ts and resolve-model (the OAuth "pose as Claude Code" path lives there).

read:playback.contracts:
OPENMAIC CONTRACTS

1. Action and Scene shapes.
- Action union: packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/action.ts:235-256.
  - Fire-and-forget: `spotlight{elementId,dimOpacity?}`, `laser{elementId,color?}`.
  - Blocking: `speech{text,audioId?,voice?,speed?}`, `wb_open`, `wb_draw_text{content,x,y,w?,h?,fontSize?,color?,elementId?}`, `wb_draw_shape`, `wb_draw_chart{chartType,data{labels,legends,series}}`, `wb_draw_latex{latex}`, `wb_draw_table{data:string[][]}`, `wb_draw_line{startX..endY,points}`, `wb_draw_code`, `wb_edit_code{operation,lineId(s)}`, `wb_clear`, `wb_delete{elementId}`, `wb_close`, `play_video{elementId}`, `discussion{topic,prompt?,agentId?}`, `widget_highlight`, `widget_setState`, `widget_annotation`, `widget_reveal`.
  - Partitions: FIRE_AND_FORGET at :261, SYNC at :267.
  - Whiteboard coordinates are 0-1000 x 0-562.
- Scene: SceneCore{id, stageId, title, order, actions?, whiteboards?, multiAgent?} with type bound to content (slide/PPTist canvas | quiz | interactive | pbl), stage.ts:228-283.
- QuizQuestion carries `answer` and `analysis` (stage.ts:196-206).

2. Model output format (live and offline are identical).
- A JSON array `[{"type":"action","name":"spotlight","params":{"elementId":"img_1"}},{"type":"text","content":"natural speech"}]`.
- Defined in prompt-builder.ts:57-66 and pi/prompts.ts:189-202.
- Live parse: stateless-generate.ts:136-255 (partial-json + jsonrepair; text deltas streamed, actions emitted in order).
- Offline parse: generation/src/action-parser.ts:41 turns it into Action[] (text becomes speech).
- Ordering rule: spotlight/laser before the text they refer to (prompt-builder.ts:60-61).

3. Live wire protocol (SSE).
- Request StatelessChatRequest, lib/types/chat.ts:340-420: messages (UIMessage), the full storeState (stage, all scenes with quiz answers, currentSceneId, whiteboardOpen, quizResults), config{agentIds, sessionType 'qa'|'discussion', discussionTopic/Prompt, triggerAgentId, agentConfigs, piMax*}, directorState, userProfile{nickname,bio}, apiKey.
- Events StatelessEvent, chat.ts:457-510: agent_start{messageId,agentId,agentName}, text_delta{content,messageId}, action{actionId,actionName,params,agentId,messageId}, thinking{stage,agentId}, whiteboard, cue_user{fromAgentId,prompt}, agent_end, done{totalActions,totalAgents,agentHadContent,cueUserReceived,sessionClosed,endReason,directorState}, error.
- Routes: /api/chat (route.ts:46) and /api/chat/pi (pi/route.ts:53), the default.

4. Directors.
- Legacy single-agent path is pure code: turn 0 dispatches the agent, turn 1+ sends cue_user (director-graph.ts:117-132). The graph is START, director, agent_generate, END (:484-496).
- Pi director tools: read_scene, call_agent, close_session, cue_user (director-loop.ts:138-215). Limits: 6 agent turns, 8 actions per agent (pi/config.ts:5-8).
- The client loops until cue_user, END or 2 empty turns (agent-loop.ts:154-269).

5. Playback engine API.
- Constructor `new PlaybackEngine(scenes, actionEngine, audioPlayer, callbacks)` (engine.ts:95). The host passes `[currentScene]`, one engine per scene (PlaybackChromeRoot.tsx:787).
- Methods: start, continuePlayback, jumpToAction(i,{autoplay}) (scene 0 only), pause, resume, stop, confirmDiscussion, skipDiscussion, handleEndDiscussion, handleDiscussionError, handleUserInterrupt(text) (saves actionIndex-1), isExhausted, hasLectureInterruption, getSnapshot/restoreFromSnapshot.
- EngineMode is 'idle'|'playing'|'paused'|'live' (types.ts:18). Snapshot is {sceneIndex, actionIndex, consumedDiscussions, sceneId} (types.ts:5-10).
- Callbacks (types.ts:32-65): onModeChange, onSceneChange, onSpeechStart(text), onSpeechEnd, onEffectFire({kind,targetId}), onProactiveShow/Hide, onDiscussionConfirmed/End, onUserInterrupt, onProgress, isAgentSelected, getPlaybackSpeed, onComplete.
- ActionEngine.execute(action,{silent,signal}) (action/engine.ts:214).

6. Timing, seek and session rules.
- Timing: effect auto-clear 5000 ms, discussion trigger 3000 ms, auto-skip 5000 ms, wb open 2000, draw 800, edit 600, delete 300, close 700, widget 300 ms (timing.ts:18-74). No-audio speech is max(2000, 240 ms per word) divided by speed (:113-121).
- Cursor: resolvePlaybackCursor(scenes, si, ai) (cursor.ts:44). Timeline: resolveActionTimeline gives TimelineSegment{startMs,durationMs,advance}.
- Session rules: soft close 15 s (use-chat-sessions.ts:48); auto-resume only on soft_close_confirmed or timeout with endReason user_done or back_to_lesson (auto-resume.ts:37-44); playback phases (derived-state.ts:38-46).

OUR CONTRACTS TO TARGET (apps/web/src)

- Content model: Lesson{id,title,summary,minutes,scenes} with Scene = slide{blocks} | quiz{questions} | interactive{prompt,widget} | project (lib/types.ts:124-130). Block, Visual and Widget unions at :66-113.
- Board: BoardCard union (lib/tutor.ts:68-88).
- Tutor request: TutorContext zod (lib/ai/context.ts:37-51). Spec 2.5 adds `input` and `spots`. scrubContext and scrubMessages remove names (:145, :160).
- Tutor turn: tutorTurn(body, model) gives a UIMessage stream (lib/ai/tutor.ts:104). Tools in lib/ai/tools.ts:72.
- Voice: SpeechOut and SpeechIn (lib/voice/types.ts:39-101). Spec 3.2 adds speak(source,{signal,kind,band}) returning a SpeechRun with an id, plus onWordScheduled(word,audibleAt,run), heardUpTo, duck/unduck, cancel({fadeMs}).
- Spec 3.1: cueParser(epoch) with push/end/cues, where Cue = {id,word,epoch}, and the anchor syntax `[[spot:<id>]]` (CUE_MARK regex).
- Spec 3.4: beginPointing({epoch,voice}) returns {move(id,{glideMs}),rest,end}. Attention epoch is `${pathname}|${item|scene|talk}|${messageId}`.

PROPOSED BRIDGE

A theater Action is a trimmed DSL:
- speech{text with anchors, clip?}
- point{spot}
- board{card: BoardCard}
- widget{kind:'set'|'reveal', ...}
- pause{ms}

A Take is {id, profileId, epoch, sceneId?, actions: Action[], words?: {i, atMs}[], source: 'live'|'demo'|'generated', createdAt}. It is stored in StoreState next to `threads`. It replays through the same engine. A replay never counts as help or as proof.
risks: Never-ship OAuth path is reachable from anything 'live'. /api/chat, /api/chat/pi and /api/quiz-grade all resolve models through lib/server/resolve-model into lib/ai/providers.ts, whose sk-ant-oat branch (providers.ts:2642-2692) and the instrumentation.ts:66-68 refresh timer are the Claude Code impersonation. Porting any route, resolve-model or providers.ts code drags it in. Port only the pure modules listed.

Learner names reach the model. prompt-builder.ts:82-87 ('Address them by name naturally'), pi/prompts.ts:209 and :267 ('User nickname: ...'), the default teacher persona 'Encourage students by name' (registry/store.ts:59), and the client sends userProfile.nickname (use-chat-sessions.ts:1683, 1878, 2002). This violates 'learner names never to a model'. Our scrubContext and scrubMessages must stay the only path.

Answer keys and model grading. The client posts the full storeState, including every quiz `answer` (lib/types/chat.ts:344-372). After submission the prompt includes 'Correct answer' and the reference analysis (state-context.ts:193-203). Short answers are graded by an LLM in /api/quiz-grade. This violates 'answers checked by code' and 'tutor prompt never contains an answer key'. Build the prompt context field by field, as the one-workspace spec section 6 requires.

No safety screen in OpenMAIC's chat routes: requests go straight from resolveModel to the director. Ours runs screen() first (lib/ai/tutor.ts:110-116). Any theater live path must go through tutorTurn, not a ported route.

Latency is incompatible with the binding spec section 2.3 (p50 1.6 s from the learner's last word to first sound, one model call per turn per section 2.5). The Pi path makes at least two serial model calls (director, then child) plus a client loop round-trip for cue_user. StreamBuffer adds postTextDelayMs 1200 and actionDelayMs 800 on purpose (use-chat-sessions.ts:924). Text-to-speech waits for a sealed segment and synthesizes it whole (use-discussion-tts.ts:243-282).

Timing granularity mismatch. OpenMAIC cues are per action (they fire just before a sentence's audio and clear themselves at 5 s), and AudioPlayer has no word timing. Spec sections 3.2-3.4 require word-level onWordScheduled with a 150 ms lead, a persistent ring never re-keyed per move, and no dim in voice mode. OpenMAIC's LaserOverlay remounts per move (keyed by centre, LaserOverlay.tsx:34) and its spotlight dims the screen. Porting the cue layer as-is fails acceptance criteria 12, 13 and 16.

'Recorded and replayable' is not a port. OpenMAIC replays generated lectures but keeps live Q&A and discussion only as chat transcripts (use-chat-sessions.ts:634-639 setChats). Recording live tutor turns as Action[] takes with word timing, plus replay, is new work. Replays must be labelled as replays and must never count as help, exposure or proof (the mastery law; practice is never proof).

Target id spaces differ. OpenMAIC points at PPTist slide element ids (screen-element-<id>) on a 1000x562 canvas; ours uses data-spot ids across the whole DOM with guards that never point at an answer. Generator output's elementIds and wb_* coordinates need remapping or re-prompting, and every target must pass guardSpots and the no-counting-along rules (spec 3.3).

Content model mismatch. OpenMAIC slides are PPTist canvases, interactive scenes are generated HTML in sandboxed iframes, and PBL is its own scene kind. Ours are Blocks, Visual and 15 typed Widgets. Using 'the OpenMAIC generator' for lessons needs a converter or a re-targeted prompt plus our lesson gates; wholesale import would drag in the PPTist renderer, echarts, katex and dexie.

Dependency and version drift. OpenMAIC uses ai ^6 and @ai-sdk/react ^3, Next 16.3.3 and React 19.2.3, plus zustand, motion, LangGraph, pi-agent-core, partial-json and jsonrepair. apps/web uses ai ^7, @ai-sdk/react ^4, Next 16.4.0, React 19.3.0 and none of those libraries. Copy-paste of SDK-touching code (ai-sdk-adapter, stream-fn, use-chat-sessions) will not compile cleanly.

Locale and copy. Upstream defaults to zh-CN; Chinese literals sit in prompts (pi/prompts.ts:113-116, 202) and agent names ('AI助教', '显眼包', registry/store.ts:74 and 98); Spanish exists only as es-MX; there are amber-to-red gradient dialogs (PlaybackChromeRoot.tsx:2053, 2076). All of it conflicts with 'no AI slop', our t() rule and EN/ES parity.

Browser speech inside the engine. PlaybackEngine calls speechSynthesis directly (engine.ts:789-876) and so does our useSpeech.ts (17-25, 78-115). Spec section 2.7 requires speechSynthesis only in lib/voice/browser.ts behind one app SpeechOut. A ported engine must take an injected SpeechOut, or 'one voice everywhere' (acceptance criterion 1) fails.

Sequencing. Spec section 0.4 says the tutor branch (worktree-wf_a6840288, tip 5cffe4c) must land before Phase 3; building the theater's recording into TutorChat earlier would fork it. The owner's 'tutor first' direction also puts live-tutor P1-P3 (voice, anchors, cursor) ahead of theater playback and generator work.

Demo mode. OpenMAIC's live mode needs a model; only pre-generated lectures play without AI. A theater must still perform without AI: code-built beats from the demo tutor (spec 3.5 hintSpotAt) and catalogue lessons with authored cues, honestly labelled.

Licence. Files copied from OpenMAIC (DSL action contract, choreography, auto-resume, action-navigation, any engine logic) must carry the MIT notice (modules/openmaic-classroom/LICENSE). AGENTS.md forbids importing from modules/: copy and adapt into apps/web/src/lib/theater instead.

Persistence. OpenMAIC needs Postgres (it throws at boot without DATABASE_URL) and keeps its resume cursor in a device KV. Takes and resume cursors need a home in our StoreState (lib/store.ts:18-40, with localStorage try/catch) and later lib/sync.ts. Storing audio is barred by the privacy rule, so replay audio must come from re-synthesis or the clip store (spec P5), never from recordings of the learner.

read:dsl-renderer.summary:
Read-only map. OpenMAIC paths are relative to /Users/man/Documents/GitHub/Tutornat/modules/openmaic-classroom. Our paths are relative to /Users/man/Documents/GitHub/Tutornat/apps/web/src unless they start with docs/. Nothing was run: the module has no node_modules or dist.

THE ANSWER IN ONE LINE: what OpenMAIC does well for a tutor-first KaizenEDU is its performance contract, not its slide canvas. Port the contract and rewrite the parts that run it on our voice clock.

1. How a scene is described. A scene is {type, content, actions[]} (packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/stage.ts:228-283). `actions` is a script of 21 verbs (action.ts:235-256): speech, spotlight/laser, the whiteboard draw/edit/clear verbs, discussion and widget_*. The live agent uses the same verbs (lib/chat/pi/tools/native-whiteboard.ts), and PlaybackEngine replays them offline (lib/playback/engine.ts). That is the owner's "live theater, recorded and replayable": a lesson is a recorded tutor performance, and the live tutor plays the same script one reply at a time.

2. How a scene is drawn.
- **Slides** are PPTist-style absolute canvases, 1000×562.5 (generation/src/scene-builder.ts:36-63). @openmaic/renderer paints them; text and latex arrive as HTML strings injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- **Math** is KaTeX, rendered when the content is written and always with output:'html', so there is no MathML.
- **Whiteboard** is a second Slide that the tutor adds elements to. There is no freehand ink anywhere.
- **Quiz:** single/multiple are graded by code; short_answer is graded by a model.
- **Interactive:** a model-written HTML page in a sandboxed iframe. The widget_* commands only work if that generated page implements them itself.
- **PBL** is about 17k lines of multi-agent workspace graded by models.

3. Sync is per segment, not per word. A spotlight fires before a speech action and clears itself after 5 s. Each draw blocks the next action for 0.8-2 s. Speech waits for its audio to end. Our spec §3.1-3.3 binds cues to words with the voice as the clock, so the executors (lib/action/engine.ts, lib/playback/engine.ts) must be rewritten, not copied.

4. What to port:
- the verb vocabulary, mapped onto our cues and board ops;
- the pure choreography (lib/choreography/cursor.ts, timeline.ts) for replay;
- the whiteboard op-log and fold (lib/whiteboard/runtime/*) for recorded sessions;
- the playback patterns: interrupt goes live and resumes at the interrupted sentence; seek silently replays board ops; stale async work is dropped by an epoch check;
- a trimmed copy (about 1.2k lines) of the renderer's text/shape/line/latex/table/image painters, for the tutor's board only.

5. What to leave: the editor (16.7k lines), PBL, the iframe interactives (our workspace spec says the model may not run JavaScript), model-graded short answers, the legacy in-app renderer (12k lines), and the snapshot/fonts pipeline.

6. Decision for "use the OpenMAIC generator". Its pipeline (outline → content → actions) is solid. Its slide output is our worst fit:
- on a 320 px phone the canvas scales to about 0.29-0.32, so 18 px text shows at about 5-6 px;
- images get alt="" and nothing supports reduced motion;
- it stamps an Office palette and Microsoft YaHei;
- the words on the slide are not the words the voice says.

My recommendation:
- (A) Keep its outlines and actions, but have the slide-content step write our Block/Visual JSON so lessons render on our Stage. Map each spotlight→speech pair to a [[spot:id]] anchor at word 0.
- (B) Use the ported canvas painters only for the tutor's 16:9 board, beside the work, not over it.

Also worth knowing: OpenMAIC's own playback still defaults to the legacy renderer. @openmaic/renderer is behind NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIC_PLAYBACK_RENDERER_ENABLED, which is off by default (lib/config/feature-flags.ts:75-81), so the package is less proven in playback than it looks.

7. License and the OAuth path. OpenMAIC changed from AGPL-3.0 to MIT at v0.3.0 (UPSTREAM_README.md:69), so keep its MIT notice. Check where the PPTist-derived slide model and renderer came from before copying them word for word. A grep of the rendering, DSL, choreography, whiteboard, quiz and playback code found no reference to the Anthropic OAuth adapter.

2. SLIDE (dsl/src/slides.ts:995-1011)
- Slide{id, viewportSize: 1000, viewportRatio: 0.5625, theme{backgroundColor, themeColors[], fontColor, fontName}, elements: PPTElement[], background?, animations?}.
- Element base{id, left, top, width, height, rotate} (156-167).
- Kinds: text{content: HTML} (210), image{src} (332), shape{path, viewBox} (432), line{start, end, points: [''|'arrow'|'dot']} (480), chart{chartType, data{labels, legends, series}} (572), table{data: TableCell[][]} (716), latex{latex, html} (753), video, audio, code{lines{id, content}[]} (853).

- Whiteboard = Omit<Slide, 'theme' | 'turningMode' | 'sectionTag' | 'type'> (stage.ts:51).

3. ACTION TIMELINE (dsl/src/action.ts:235-287)
- Scene.actions is an ordered script. spotlight and laser are fire-and-forget; every other verb blocks.
- The generator writes [{type:'action', name:'spotlight', params:{elementId}}, {type:'text', content}] with the spotlight before its speech (templates/slide-actions/system.md). action-parser keeps only allowed verbs and never checks that an elementId exists.
- Executor (lib/action/engine.ts:214-284):
  - spotlight/laser set the canvas store, then clear after 5000 ms (lib/choreography/timing.ts:18).
  - speech resolves when its audio ends (336-350).
  - wb_open waits 2000 ms, each draw 800 ms, wb_draw_code 800 + 50 ms per line (cap 3000), wb_clear 380 + 55 ms per element (cap 1400), widget_* 300 ms (timing.ts:43-74).
  - Speech with no audio is estimated at 240 ms per word, minimum 2 s (timing.ts:113-121).
- Cursor: resolvePlaybackCursor(scenes, si, ai) → {action, sceneId, sceneIndex, actionIndex} | null (cursor.ts:44-73).
- Index→time: resolveActionTimeline (timeline.ts).
- Speech cue group: the contiguous spotlight/laser actions just before a speech belong to it (lib/playback/action-navigation.ts:49-60).
- Seek: silently re-run whiteboard verbs up to the target speech (engine.ts:185-215).
- Interrupt: saved = actionIndex − 1, then mode becomes live (engine.ts:442-470).
- PlaybackSnapshot{sceneIndex, actionIndex, consumedDiscussions, sceneId} (lib/playback/types.ts:5-10).

4. RENDER API (packages/@openmaic/renderer/src/SlideCanvas.tsx:27-87)
- Props: SlideCanvas{slide, scale?, canvasPercentage?, onScaleChange?, effects?: SlideEffects, renderImage?, renderVideo?, renderText?, renderShapeLabel?, renderTable?, onElementClick?, elementIdPrefix = 'slide-element-', hiddenElementIds?, dragOffsets?, chrome?}.
- SlideEffects{laser?{elementId, color, duration}, spotlight?{elementId, dimness}, highlight(s)?{elementId, color, opacity, borderWidth, animated}, zoom?{elementId, scale}} (types/effects.ts:1-31).
- Element DOM: <div class="slide-element" id={prefix+id} style="position:absolute; inset:0; z-index: order"> wrapping .rotate-wrapper and .element-content (SlideElement.tsx:163-197). Spotlight measures .element-content (SpotlightOverlay.tsx:44-45).
- OpenMAIC's own app prefixes: 'screen-element-' / 'editable-element-' plus data-maic-element-id (components/slide-renderer/element-dom.ts).

5. WHITEBOARD RUNTIME (lib/whiteboard/runtime/types.ts:19-96)
- WhiteboardRuntimePayloadV1{payloadVersion: 1, operationId, operation: legacy_snapshot_imported | element_added{element} | element_deleted{elementId} | elements_cleared | code_lines_edited{elementId, edit}}.
- Append input {stageId, expectedLastSeq, payload} → {committedSeq, state{sessionId, whiteboard, lastSeq}, replayed}.
- The record type is RuntimeRecord<payload> from dsl/src/runtime.ts (seq assigned by the store; timestamps are ISO strings).
- Live tool: Pi wb_draw_* with strict arguments plus wb_read (lib/chat/pi/tools/native-whiteboard.ts:335-348, 669, 743+). Element ids are `native-wb-element:<sha256>`.

6. INTERACTIVE BRIDGE
- Parent → iframe: postMessage({type: 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT' | 'SET_WIDGET_STATE' | 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT' | 'REVEAL_ELEMENT', target | state, content}, '*') (engine.ts:863-901; InteractiveIframeHost.tsx:316).
- Iframe → parent: observation reports (≤32 KB, depth ≤64, lib/interactive/observation.ts:3-13).

7. QUIZ GRADING
- gradeChoiceQuestions(questions, answers) → QuestionResult{questionId, correct, status, earned} (lib/quiz/grading.ts:67-89).
- short_answer → POST /api/quiz-grade {question, userAnswer, points, commentPrompt, language} (quiz-view.tsx:92-110).

8. OUR BINDING SIDE
- SPOT_ID = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,63}$/ and spotAttr(id, label) (lib/spotlight.ts:16-27); visibleSpots (263), resolveSpot (278), guardSpots (307).
- Cue anchors: [[spot:<id>]] placed before a word; the cue fires at audibleAt − 150 ms; glide clamp(240 + 0.3 × px, 280, 560) ms; dwell ≥ 900 ms (1200 ms K-2); at most 5 moves per reply; no counting along; epoch `${pathname}|${item|scene|talk}|${messageId}` (docs/plans/2026-10-07-live-tutor-spec.md §3.1-3.4, lines 618-790).
- Narration cues: `cues?: {seg, spot, word?}[]`, plus automatic stage.block.<i>.visual.<kind> (§3.5, lines 792-812).
- Latency: last word to first sound p50 ≤ 1.6 s (§2.3, lines 366-395).
- Board tools are echo-only and come after the words (§2.5, lines 473-505).

9. PROPOSED TRANSLATION
- spotlight(X) or laser(X) followed by speech(T) → a speech segment T with cue {spot: stage.slide.<slug(X)>, word: 0}.
- highlight → the ring with no cursor.
- zoom → leave.
- The whiteboard draw verbs → BoardOp{kind: text | math | shape | line | table | visual, id, ...}, applied by a pure reducer and stored as seq-ordered session records; replay is a fold.
- discussion → hand off to the live tutor (playing → live), then resume at the saved sentence.
- widget_setState → a typed per-Widget command (e.g. number-line {start}); never a selector.
- Generator element ids such as 'text_001' must be slugged ('_' fails SPOT_ID) and checked against the slide before use.
risks: License provenance: the slide model and renderer look derived from PPTist. Evidence: Chinese PPTist-style type comments (dsl/src/slides.ts:63-72), ShapePathFormulasKeys, the .rotate-wrapper/.element-content DOM, and the README's 'PPTist-style Slide JSON'. To my knowledge PPTist is AGPL-3.0; verify that. OpenMAIC itself changed from AGPL-3.0 to MIT only at v0.3.0 (UPSTREAM_README.md:69). Before copying slides.ts or the element painters word for word, confirm where they came from. Keep the THU-MAIC MIT notice, and never port packages/mathml2omml (LGPL-3.0).

XSS: the renderer injects text and latex HTML with dangerouslySetInnerHTML (BaseTextElement.tsx:39, BaseLatexElement.tsx:162). OpenMAIC sanitizes only when content is stored (lib/server/classroom-persistence.ts:20). The legacy wb_draw_text path passes any model content starting with '<' straight into the DOM (lib/action/engine.ts:481-483). Any port must sanitize at our tutor route and lesson gate, or render text as text.

Phones: a fixed 1000×562 canvas at 320 px scales to about 0.29-0.32, so the generator's 18 px body text shows at about 5-6 px. That breaks our 320 px rule. Unmodified generator slides cannot be the lesson surface on phones.

Accessibility gaps everywhere in the slide stack: images get alt="" (BaseImageElement.tsx:78); the DSL has no alt or description fields; KaTeX output:'html' means no MathML; nothing supports reduced motion (infinite laser pulse, highlight ping, whiteboard blur/rotate cascade); whiteboard pan is pointer-only; audio aria labels are English only. Each conflicts with AGENTS.md rule 5.

Sync granularity: OpenMAIC binds attention to a whole speech segment (spotlight before speech, cleared after 5 s) and draws block the next speech for 0.8-2 s. Our sync contract (spec §3) is per word, with the voice as the clock, a ring that holds through the learner's turn, and a 1.6 s first-sound budget. Copying lib/action/engine.ts or lib/playback/engine.ts would break that contract. The laser also lands at 5% + 0.9 × centre (SlideCanvas.tsx:248-268), missing small edge targets.

Spot ids: generator element ids like 'text_001' fail SPOT_ID because underscores are not allowed (lib/spotlight.ts:16). Renderer roots carry a DOM id, not data-spot. Neither the validators (dsl validate.ts:243-297) nor the action parser check that spotlight targets exist. Cues must be slugged, validated against the slide and guarded, or they will silently light nothing or point at answers.

Answers checked by a model: short_answer (quiz-view.tsx:92-110), the PBL evaluators and iframe activities all produce model judgments. Porting any of them as evidence breaks 'answers are checked by code' and 'practice is never proof'. Demo mode must work without them.

Iframe interactives: there is no CSP, so model-written pages can fetch outside hosts; allow-popups is set; the url fallback loads any address; learner input could leave the device; our spotlight cannot see inside. The workspace spec rules out arbitrary generated code for this release.
Privacy: renderer/fonts.css pulls fonts from https://file.maic.chat. Importing it sends requests from children's devices to an outside server.

Dependency weight versus Ponytail. apps/web currently has no motion, katex, tinycolor2, lucide, echarts, shiki or sanitize-html. A naive renderer port drags most of these in; the editor would add 11 ProseMirror packages and immer. Port only the painter subset and cut motion.

Proven-ness: OpenMAIC's playback runs on the legacy in-app renderer (12k lines) by default; @openmaic/renderer is behind NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIC_PLAYBACK_RENDERER_ENABLED, which is off (lib/config/feature-flags.ts:75-81). The package has 55 tests and less real playback mileage than the duplicate it replaces.

Look: the generator stamps an Office palette ('#5b9bd5', '#ed7d31', …), 'Microsoft YaHei' and a red outline theme (generation/src/scene-builder.ts:36-63), and the whiteboard uses blur and rotate flourishes. Without re-theming to DESIGN.md this is the generic-deck, AI-slop look the owner bans.

Narration model mismatch: OpenMAIC's speech text is a script that differs from the words on the slide (slides are 'visual aids, not scripts'). Our stage reads the on-screen words aloud with word highlights, which matters for K-2 read-along. Adopting generator speech needs a caption or transcript surface and element cues, or a slide-content variant that writes our blocks.

Model round trips: the Pi whiteboard tools require wb_read plus expectedLastSeq before each mutation. That adds model steps against spec §2.5 'one model call per turn' and the latency budget. Use echo-only board tools that the client applies in order instead.

OAuth adapter: the rendering, DSL, choreography, whiteboard, quiz and playback code has no reference to anthropic-oauth, sk-ant-oat or claude-code (grep). But lib/action/engine.ts and lib/playback/engine.ts import app stores and settings. Port file by file and never copy lib/ai/*, lib/server/anthropic-oauth-refresh.ts or instrumentation.ts.
