design:1.name: Our Stage, Their Brain: the KaizenEDU tutor theater
design:1.thesis:
The theater is one recorded form: a list of Beats bound to a scene. Each beat holds words to say, cues tied to a word index, an optional typed widget demonstration, and an optional handover of the turn to the learner. Three producers write beats and one player performs them.

The producers:
- **The live tutor:** `[[spot:id]]` anchors, run through `cueParser`.
- **OpenMAIC's script writer, ported:** its `generateSceneActions` contract, prompts and spotlight-before-speech timeline, rewritten as `writeScript` with structured output whose spot field is a `z.enum` of the scene's own spot ids.
- **Code:** built from the scene data. It is the demo, the fallback and K–2 read-along.

The player runs on our Stage, our widgets, our spotlight and ring/cursor, and our single SpeechOut, with the voice as the clock. Nothing from OpenMAIC's surface ships: no PPT canvas, no iframe HTML, no directors, no audio stack, no provider or OAuth code. We take their brain (the pipeline shape, prompts and action-timeline model), not their stage.

Order follows the owner:
1. Wire the live tutor (live-tutor spec P1–P3).
2. Put it on the stage as a player.
3. Record every session so it can be replayed.
4. Only then let the ported generator write scripts for every lesson, and let sessions become new lessons.

Lessons are what the tutor makes. The performances (live, recorded, replayed) are what stays.

**Correction to the code maps:** the tutor branch is not a blocker. Its content is already on foundation: `git cherry foundation 5cffe4c` gives 17 patch-identical commits, and the other two landed reworked as 9dd173f and db9a916. What actually blocks is the spec pieces missing on HEAD:
- no `lib/voice/player.ts`, `lib/voice/cues.ts` or `lib/attention.ts`;
- `SpotlightLayer` is not mounted;
- no `data-spot` outside the spotlight module;
- `point_at` still exists in `spot-tool.ts`, though it is not in `tutorTools`.
design:1.tutorFirst:
## 0. Order

The tutor is wired before any script is generated. The live-tutor spec P1–P3 lands first, because the theater has no clock without it:
- `numbers.ts` / `speakable`, `voices.ts`, `audio.ts`, `player.ts`;
- `VoiceRoot` as the one audio owner;
- `conversation.ts`, Flux / Nova, barge-in;
- `cues.ts`, `attention.ts`, the pointing session, ring and TutorCursor;
- `SpotlightLayer` mounted;
- `point_at` and `runSpotFromToolPart` deleted, with anchors in their place (spec §1.3: each `point_at` cost a model step, 0.6–1.2 s of silence);
- `spotsPrompt` rewritten as the anchor guide.

The theater then reuses exactly that loop on three surfaces.

## 1. The three surfaces

**(a) Talk** (`app/(focus)/talk`, TutorChat + Board):
- The reply streams through `cueParser` and is spoken through the app SpeechOut.
- Anchors light `tutor.*`, `board.visual.*` (latest card only) and `nav.*`.
- `show_visual` and the other echo-only board tools come after the words (`stopWhen`: last step all BOARD_TOOLS).
- Each reply is recorded as a take: tutor.say beats plus the board card.
- New in the theater phase: a "Make a lesson about X" board card (echo-only `make_lesson`). It needs a tap; nothing is spent without one.

**(b) The drawer beside a problem** (TutorDrawer + Runner):
- Anchors point at `practice.prompt.part.*` and `practice.visual.*`.
- `guardSpots(answerSpots(item))` plus the value-part prefixes from spec §5.3.
- The demo tutor's hint replies are code-built beats with `hintSpotAt(item, rung)` cues.
- On Next: the drawer closes, speech and cues are cancelled, the epoch changes.
- A spoken answer goes through the server precheck (`spoken.ts`) and never through the model's judgement.

**(c) The lesson stage** (Stage.tsx):
- The header gains Play. Play runs the scene's Script (AI if present, else authored, else `codeScript`) through `player.ts`.
- Key-bound beats highlight words in place through `Spoken`; other beats show in Caption.
- The whiteboard button, now "opens when the tutor is connected" (Stage.tsx `boardNote`), becomes the Board beside the scene. It never covers the work.
- **Interrupt:** a mic tap, a typed message, or a touch on any control (pointerdown or keydown on an interactive element):
  - ducks within 150 ms and stops within 800 ms;
  - cancels pending cues;
  - the player saves the cut beat and enters `live`.
- **The live turn:** tutorTurn with `surface: 'lesson'` and `observation` = `publicObservation(scene, live)`, which carries the widget's current value and no target or quiz key. It also sends:
  - `spots` = `sceneSpots ∩ visibleSpots`;
  - `heard` = the heard prefix of the cut beat plus " [interrupted]" (spec §2.4 truncation, in `prepareSendMessagesRequest`).
  It is one model call.
- **After the live turn:** a "Keep going" chip (voice: "keep going" / "sigue") resumes at the cut beat from its first word.
- **On a `wait` beat:** the player stops and the learner acts.
  - The widget's `onCheck` or the quiz answer is checked by code, as today.
  - The verdict reaches the tutor as text ("checker: not yet"), never as a key.
  - The live tutor (or the demo tutor's vetted hint) answers, then the script continues or the scene ends.
- **A `show` beat** animates the real widget state through the adapter (controlled widgets only), then resets to the learner's start. It counts as help: `memory.help(checkIds(scene))`.

## 2. Live sync contract (binding, from spec §3)

**One word space:** `display.split(/\s+/)`. The chunker splits only at whitespace, and `replyText()` is the only place markers are stripped.

**Voice clock:**
- `speak()` returns a SpeechRun with an id.
- `onWordScheduled(word, audibleAt, run)` gives `audibleAt` = alignment start + outputLatency.
- Prebuffer: 150 ms or 250 ms, whichever comes first. Scheduling lead: 50 ms.
- `heardUpTo()` gives the truncation point.
- Browser voices: `onBoundary` only, with a 200 ms glide.
- Voice off: a cue fires when its word or beat renders. No simulated word timing.

**Attention:**
- The cursor arrives 150 ms before the word.
- Glide = clamp(240 + 0.3 × px, 280, 560) ms, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)`.
- Late cues: up to 300 ms late, glide in the remaining time (minimum 160 ms). Later, crossfade in 150 ms while the sentence still plays. Once the sentence has ended, drop the cue.
- Dwell ≥ 900 ms (1200 ms K–2). At most 5 moves per reply or per played scene, and at most 3 anchors per reply.
- No counting along in indexed families while the item is unanswered.
- At fire time: the epoch matches, `resolveSpot` finds it, `isShown`, and not guarded. A missing target is retried every 100 ms until its sentence ends.

**Epochs:**
- Live: `${pathname}|${item|scene|talk}|${messageId}`.
- Played: `${pathname}|${scene.id}|play:${script.hash}`.
- An epoch change cancels everything.

**Glow:**
- One ring per pointing session (per reply, or per played scene run), never re-keyed. It tweens to the live rect each frame with rAF.
- Arrival is a 220 ms bloom; the two pulses play on the first arrival only.
- The ring holds through the learner's turn, rests at 6 s (60% opacity, no glow), and clears on the learner's next action, Escape, or a change of item, scene or route.
- Voice mode has no dim and no captions.

**Cursor:**
- A 14 px `--color-accent` dot with a 2 px panel ring. Never arrow-shaped, `aria-hidden`.
- It parks 4 px outside the ring. If its path crosses a guarded box or is longer than 60% of the viewport diagonal, it fades out and in instead of travelling.
- Poses: at `[data-tutor-mic]` while listening; one glide to the learner's committed bubble or the pad output while thinking; at `[data-tutor-home]` (the newest bubble, the Play button on the stage, or BigHear) while speaking without anchors.
- Reduced motion: no dot, a 150 ms ring crossfade at word time. Forced colors: the dashed Highlight ring.

**`point_at`:** retired in favour of anchors, which cost no extra call. `SpotAgain` replays a message's or beat's cues with dwell spacing and no audio.

**Theater numbers (new, on top of spec §2.3):**

| Measure | Target |
|---|---|
| Play tap → visible acknowledgement (cursor to home, first caption) | ≤ 150 ms |
| Play tap → first sound, clip | p50 ≤ 250 ms |
| Play tap → first sound, Tier A browser voice | p50 ≤ 400 ms |
| Play tap → first sound, vendor (socket pre-opened on the stage after consent and a gesture) | p50 ≤ 700 ms |
| Gap between beats | Band pauses only (one `speak()` per scene run, no per-beat request) |
| Live answer on the stage, 3–9 | p50 ≤ 1.6 s, p90 ≤ 2.5 s |
| Live answer on the stage, K–2 | p50 ≤ 2.4 s |
| "Keep going" → first sound | p50 ≤ 700 ms |

Generation never runs inside a turn.
design:1.recording:
## What a recording is

A `TheaterSession` with an append-only log of `TheaterRecord`s. The shape follows OpenMAIC's `dsl` `runtime.ts`: records are ordered by a store-assigned seq (never by timestamps), and anchors may go stale.

```ts
TheaterSession = {
  id; profileId;
  surface: 'talk' | 'drawer' | 'lesson';
  courseId?; lessonId?;
  startedAt; endedAt?;
  status: 'active' | 'done';
  v: 1;
  kept?: boolean;
}

TheaterRecord = {
  seq;
  at;        // ms from session start
  anchor?: { sceneId?: string; itemKey?: string };
  r: ...     // one of the kinds below
}
```

Record kinds (`r`):

| Kind | Fields |
|---|---|
| `tutor.say` | `run`, `text` (display, markers stripped, names scrubbed), `cues: {spot, word}[]`, `w: number[]` (delta-encoded word onsets in ms, relative to run start; empty for browser voices without boundaries), `heard` (`heardUpTo` at the end), `cut?`, `src: 'live' \| 'demo' \| 'script'`, `scriptHash?`, `beat?` |
| `learner.turn` | `via: 'voice' \| 'text' \| 'chip'`, `text` (scrubbed on the device by `scrubNames` before storage). Never audio. |
| `check` | `checkId`, `verdict: 'right' \| 'not-yet'`, `assisted` (copied from the code checker's record; display only) |
| `widget.state` | `kind`, `state` (a public snapshot after each learner change or `show`; idempotent `opId`) |
| `board.card` | `BoardCard` |
| `stage.scene` | `sceneId` |
| `safety` | `kind` (the referral shown, not the text) |
| `mark` | `voice: 'vendor' \| 'tierA' \| 'tierB' \| 'off'`, `descriptor: 'ring.v1'`, so an old replay renders as it was recorded |

**Recorder:** `lib/theater/record.ts` subscribes to `player.ts`, the TutorChat message stream (via `replyText` plus cues) and SpeechOut `onWordScheduled` / `heardUpTo`.

**Storage:**
- IndexedDB `kaizenedu.theater`, beside `blobs.ts`, never the localStorage document.
- About 0.4 KB per tutor line, so a 20-minute session is ≤ 64 KB.
- Per learner: at most 8 MB and 200 sessions. Sessions older than 90 days are pruned unless `kept`.
- `lib/export.ts` includes sessions, and deleting a learner deletes them.
- Sync through `lib/sync.ts` later, under the same export/delete rules.

## How it replays

`/replay/[id]`, and "Watch again" on transcripts (the child page and Family) and on a finished lesson. Replay runs the same `player.ts` in replay mode.

**With the original voice:**
- **Catalogue and code lines:** the P5 clip store, `voice/<sha256(text|voice|model|speed)[:16]>.{mp3,json}`, holds the original audio with alignment. Cues use the recorded alignment exactly.
- **Live replies:** audio is kept only if a grown-up turns on "Keep the tutor's voice with replays".
  - The source is the tutor output bus, after the GainNode and never the mic, recorded through `MediaStreamDestination` + `MediaRecorder` as opus at about 16 kbps (about 120 KB/min).
  - Clips get allocated random ids, are private, follow the same retention, and cover the tutor only.
  - Cues are scheduled from the recorded `w` onsets against the clip's playback time.

**Without it** (the default for live sessions):
- Each `tutor.say` is re-synthesized through the current app SpeechOut: the vendor voice with consent, else Tier A, else text only.
- The new voice's `onWordScheduled` is the clock, so cues stay word-true even though the timing differs from the original.
- In text-only mode, beats reveal one at a time on Next, and cues fire on render.

**Everything else in a replay:**
- Learner turns appear as muted bubbles.
- Checks show "then: right / not yet", recorded verdicts that are never re-run.
- Widgets show recorded snapshots, through controlled widgets once that phase lands; until then, a static `VisualView` of the snapshot.
- A permanent "Replay · Tue 3:40 pm" banner.
- Replay writes nothing: no ActivityEvent, Attempt, TeachingAct, review or help.
- Seek uses `timeline.ts` over recorded durations. Seeking past a learner's widget manipulation only jumps to the snapshot.

## How it becomes a reusable lesson

**1. A played lesson is already reusable.** Its `Scene.script` lives on the scene. The record only references `scriptHash` and beat, so replay and re-play share one source.

**2. "Keep as a lesson"** from a Talk or drawer session (one tap from a grown-up or a 3–9 learner):
- `writeLessonFromSession` takes the session's board cards in order plus the tutor's `tutor.say` texts. It removes `learner.turn`, `check` and `safety` records, and any tutor line that quotes the learner's own answer (a code match against the scrubbed learner turns).
- It runs the `writeCourse` single-lesson path behind `screen` → `gateWritten` → `gateLesson`, then `writeScript` per scene.
- Output: a Course with `origin 'generated'`, `ai: true` and `from: {session}`, labelled "Made with the tutor".
- It stays with the family: never cached (`remember` skipped) and never shared.

**3. "Teach it another way"** re-runs `writeScript` on a scene with an `angle` taken from TeachingPrefs (`representation`, `leadWith`). The new script is a new take; the old one is kept and selectable.

## How lessons multiply

- Every tutor session produces a replay, always.
- It can produce a lesson (a tap) and a practice set (existing `start_practice`).
- Every lesson the tutor makes, through `make_lesson` → `writeCourse`, gets scripts, first scene first. The first lesson is playable as soon as it streams in, with `codeScript`, and its AI script swaps in at the next scene boundary.
- Every played script produces takes, and the best take can become that family's default script for the scene. "Best" is a code rule: no interrupt, and the following check came out right unassisted.
- Shareable across families: only catalogue scripts (human-reviewed) and scripts on shareable cached courses (same `courseKey` cache as `cachedCourse`). Scripts carry no learner fields at all, because `writeScript` sees only the scene.
- Never shared: sessions, takes, and lessons made from sessions.
design:1.honesty:
## Labels (i18n EN/ES, never hidden)

| Where | Label |
|---|---|
| Scene with an AI script | "Narration written by AI" (small, under the Play bar) |
| Catalogue scene with a reviewed AI script | "Written by people · narration by AI, reviewed" |
| Code script | No narration label (it reads the lesson's own words) |
| Lessons the tutor made | "Written by AI" (existing `ai: true`) |
| Lessons kept from a session | "Made with the tutor" |
| Demo tutor | "demo tutor", said once in the opening (spec §2.5) |
| Replays | Persistent "Replay · <date>" banner |
| Recorded verdicts in a replay | "then: …" |
| Voice in use | "Using this device's voice" when a browser voice is used; "Voice is off for now. The words are on screen." on failure |

## Practice, not proof

- The theater never writes proof.
- Lesson checks keep flowing through the existing `onAnswer` → `record('quiz_answered', {assisted})` and the mastery law (`learning/engine.ts` constants unchanged).
- **What counts as help:**
  - Playing neutral narration of on-screen words is not help (one-workspace spec §5).
  - A `show` demonstration, a live tutor turn while the scene is open, or a cue that points into the problem counts as help for that scene's checks (`memory.help`). It is recorded before the next teaching is delivered.
- Replays and "Show me again" never count as help, exposure or attempts.

## Answers checked by code

- Right/wrong comes only from widget `check()`, the quiz index and practice `check_answer` / `spoken.ts`.
- The tutor receives verdicts as text and never keys.
- `publicObservation` is built field by field; it never spreads Widget, quiz or Item objects.
- `gateScript` code-checks that:
  - quiz beats never contain choice text or answer values and carry no cues;
  - `show` never sets a widget to or past its target while it is unanswered (`revealsAnswer` per kind; a property test covers every catalogue widget);
  - cues never touch `stage.choice.*`, `widget.answer`, `practice.pad.*` or value-part families while they are open.
- The `z.enum` makes an invented target impossible at decode time, and `guardSpots` re-checks at fire time.

## Demo mode (no AI)

Everything plays:
- `codeScript` for every scene;
- automatic visual cues;
- the demo tutor's vetted-hint beats with `hintSpotAt` cues;
- recording and replay;
- Tier A or Tier B voices, or text only.

`/api/ai/script` returns 503 and the client keeps `codeScript`. No feature disappears; it just reads the lesson's words instead of teaching around them.

## Safety

- `screen()` runs before every model call: `tutorTurn` already does.
- Fixes before any generation (P0):
  - add `screen(goal)` to `app/api/ai/course/route.ts`;
  - add `screen` on the scene text in `/api/ai/script`;
  - switch `lib/generate.ts:104` from plain `fetch` to `aiFetch`, so family names in the goal are scrubbed.
- Model-written `say` passes `screen()` before a child hears it; a failing beat is dropped.
- The quiz answer-safety block ships verbatim in the script prompt.
- Discussion and fake classmates are removed.
- Rate limit and spend: `limited` + `spendGate('course')` + `meter`, with at most 2 retries per scene.

## Privacy

- Learner names never reach a model:
  - `TutorContext` has no name;
  - `scrubContext` and `scrubMessages`;
  - `writeScript` receives scene content only, with no `userProfile`, nickname or bio (unlike OpenMAIC's slide-actions template);
  - session-to-lesson strips learner turns first.
- Recordings stay on the device, scrubbed at record time.
- No learner audio, ever. Tutor audio is kept only on opt-in.
- Recordings are covered by export and delete.
- Metrics send numbers only (`/api/voice/metric`).
- Vendor TTS and STT follow the consent rules for under-13s; clips cover learners without consent.

## Never ship

- Nothing from OpenMAIC `lib/ai/*`, `lib/server/resolve-model`, `model-config`, `providers.ts`, `anthropic-oauth*` or the `instrumentation.ts` timer.
- `npm run verify` gains a grep that fails on `sk-ant-oat|claude-code-20250219|oauth-2025-04-20|anthropicOAuth|startAnthropicOAuthRefresh|x-app: cli` under `apps/web`, plus a check that no file imports `modules/`.
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` carries THU-MAIC's MIT notice for every ported text and file.

What really blocks the theater is that spec P1-P3 is unbuilt on HEAD: there is no player.ts, cues.ts or attention.ts, SpotlightLayer is not mounted, no data-spot ids exist, and point_at is still in spot-tool.ts. Building the player before VoiceRoot and attention.ts exist would fork the voice path and bring back speechSynthesis outside browser.ts.

Read-along versus teacher speech. K-2 read-along needs the voice to say the words on screen, but OpenMAIC-style scripts deliberately say more than the slide does. Mixing them carelessly breaks the in-place word highlight. Mitigation: beats bound to on-screen text (key) highlight in place; beats without a key go to Caption. K-2 defaults to codeScript, plus AI beats only between the read segments; the owner should confirm this split.

Uncontrolled widgets. All 12 widgets keep their own useState (for example NumberLineWidget's index). Show demonstrations, replay snapshots and seek need a controlled seam. Until P7, show beats are excluded from the schema for those widgets and seek is disabled past a learner change. Refactoring 12 widgets risks regressions; the existing widgets.test.tsx and lesson-stage tests must stay green.

A generated script gives away an answer. The real failure modes are a quiz preview, pointing at the answer part, a show that sets the target, or saying the answer number. Mitigations: decode-time z.enum over pointable ids only, quiz scripts with no cues, gateScript string and number checks against choices[answer] and widget targets, and guardSpots again at fire time. The number check must also catch written-out numbers ('seven', 'siete') through numbers.ts.

Spot drift. sceneSpots (from data) can disagree with the DOM data-spot ids (from rendering), which silently lights nothing, or something unintended. The component test over every catalogue scene is mandatory, and fire-time resolveSpot drops misses silently. The enum is capped at 60 ids; a scene with more parts (a 12-part fraction plus blocks) is truncated to block-level ids.

The latency of the OpenMAIC-style pipeline does not fit a turn. The historical OpenMAIC run took over 8 minutes per scene at maximum effort. Scripts must be written in the background: they are serial with previous, maxOutputTokens 900, at modest effort, and never inside a learner turn. Play always starts on codeScript. The Vercel course route has maxDuration 300, so scripts go through their own per-scene route, not inside writeCourse.

Cost from retries and fan-out. A course of 8 lessons x 6 scenes is about 48 script calls on top of writeCourse. Every attempt is metered, there are at most 2 retries, and spendGate('course') is checked before each scene; a cap stops scripts and codeScript stays. The catalogue batch (about 1k scenes) is an offline, owner-approved run, not per family.

Prompt heritage. OpenMAIC's action prompts assume adult pacing (5-10 items per slide), a multi-agent discussion, Chinese stage-direction examples and a 'verbalize all math' TTS rule that contradicts our speakable. The port must rewrite them: band-specific beat caps, no discussion or agents, normal math notation plus the dev assertion that no raw symbol reaches the voice. Golden-snapshot the prompt so drift is visible.

Two sync formats could survive. The live path uses [[spot:id]] anchors; generated scripts use look{spot,on}. Both must convert into one Beat/Cue form with one word space (display.split(/\s+/)) and one scheduler. If a second parser or a per-format scheduler appears, live, played and replayed sessions will drift. Enforce this with a single toBeats() and a test that each producer's output round-trips.

Recording privacy and storage. Recordings of a child's tutoring sessions are sensitive. They stay on the device (IndexedDB), scrubbed at record time, with no learner audio, under export/delete coverage and with retention caps. Opt-in tutor audio needs consent wording the owner approves. localStorage must not be used: the store is one whole document and would hit its quota. Syncing recordings to the server is deferred until consent and retention are settled.

Replay honesty. A replay can look like teaching. It must not count as help, exposure or proof; it must always carry the banner and show recorded verdicts as 'then'. Re-synthesized voice changes word timing, so cues must follow the new voice clock, never recorded times on a different voice. A store-diff test guards against any writes.

The client-sent scene in /api/ai/script is an injection surface. For generated courses the scene lives only in the browser. Mitigations: SceneSchema re-parse, gateLesson, screen() on the text, size caps, and the gated output; catalogue scenes are rebuilt on the server from ids. A malicious client can only waste its own spend budget.

Expectation gap on 'use the OpenMAIC generator'. We use its pipeline shape, contracts, prompts and action-timeline model, but not its slide canvas or HTML widget content: they fail at 320 px, carry alt="", allow arbitrary JavaScript, and are ruled out by one-workspace spec §6-7. The owner should explicitly confirm 'their brain, our stage', or say they want the PPT and interactive outputs, which would bring the renderer, sandboxing and PPTist licence checks.

Review load and labelling. About 670 catalogue slide scripts written by AI need a human pass before their label can say 'reviewed'. Until then they are labelled 'Narration written by AI', or catalogue lessons stay on codeScript. 'Written by people' must never cover AI narration silently.

Licence and OAuth contamination. Every ported text and file needs THU-MAIC's MIT notice. Copying any OpenMAIC route, callLLM, resolve-model or providers.ts code brings in the Claude Code impersonation adapter. The verify grep and the no-modules-import check are the backstop and must be in place before any port lands (P0).

design:2.architecture:
Paths are under apps/web/src unless noted. Nothing is imported from modules/; ported files are copies with the THU-MAIC MIT header and are listed in apps/web/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

1. THE ONE CONTRACT: lib/theater/types.ts (new, about 60 lines)
```ts
type Cue = { spot: string /* SPOT_ID */; word: number };
type StageCmd =
  | { op: "scene"; scene: Scene }                 // put a scene on the stage or board
  | { op: "goto"; sceneId: string }               // lesson surface: a visited scene only
  | { op: "board"; card: BoardCard }              // lib/tutor.ts BoardCard
  | { op: "widget"; target: string; state: WidgetState }; // scripts only, show scenes only, never the widget being answered
type Beat = {
  id: string; say: string; cues?: Cue[];
  do?: (StageCmd & { word?: number })[];          // fires at that word; scripts default to 0, live cards fire after the words
  read?: string;                                  // narration segment key: say === the on-screen text, so the word highlight is on screen (K–2 read-along)
  wait?: "tap" | "act";                           // act = park until the scene's own checker reports
  by: "ai" | "demo" | "author" | "code";
};
```
- `Scene` (lib/types.ts:124-128) gains `script?: Beat[]`.
- Word space = `say.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)`, the same space as spec §3.1, chunk.ts, onBoundary and onWordScheduled.
- OpenMAIC's `[{type:'text'}|{type:'action'}]` arrays never enter apps/web. Its "spotlight then speech" pair is exactly a cue at word 0.

2. PRODUCERS, all turning their output into Beat (pure, unit-tested)
- **Live AI turn.** tutorTurn (lib/ai/tutor.ts, one streamText call) → useChat parts → replyText()/cueParser (spec §3.1) plus cardsOf (components/tutor/cards.ts) → `beatOf(message)` in lib/theater/beat.ts.
- **Demo tutor.** DemoTurn {text, cards} plus hintSpotAt (spec §3.5) → `demoBeat()`.
- **Generated.** `writeScript(scene, ctx, model)` in lib/theater/script.ts is OpenMAIC's generateSceneActions rewritten:
  - `Output.object` with Zod `{beats: 2..8 of {say ≤ 220 chars, cues ≤ 2 of {spot: z.enum(pointableSpots(scene)), word}, wait?}}`, so an invalid or guarded target cannot be decoded;
  - then `gateScript`;
  - on failure, the code fallback below, in the learner's locale.
- **Catalogue and fallback.** `codeScript(scene)` comes from narration.tsx slideSegments: one `read` beat per segment, the automatic `v{i}` → `stage.block.<i>.visual.<kind>` cue at word 0, and the interactive prompt plus `wait:"act"`. Quiz scenes get one i18n meta line plus `wait:"act"`.

3. CONSUMERS
- **Player: lib/theater/player.ts** (pure, about 200 lines, fake-clock tests). Modes are idle, playing, waiting, paused, live and ended. The cursor is {scene, beat}. For each beat:
  - apply each `do` at its word's audibleAt − 150 ms (the cue lead);
  - `speak(say, {kind, signal})` returns a SpeechRun;
  - feed the cues through onWordScheduled to lib/attention.ts, then to beginPointing;
  - on `wait:"act"`, park until onAnswer or onCheck fires;
  - on interrupt, save the start of the sentence holding `heardUpTo()` (finer than OpenMAIC's actionIndex − 1) and switch to live;
  - drop stale callbacks with a generation token (OpenMAIC engine.ts:495-502);
  - take a snapshot before advancing.
  - The epoch is `${pathname}|${scene.id}|${beat.id}`.
- **Cursor: lib/theater/cursor.ts.** Port of choreography/cursor.ts:44-73 (walking across scenes, dwell on an empty scene) and playback/action-navigation.ts seek safety: stage and board commands can be rebuilt silently; widget state only from recorded snapshots.
- **Stage dispatcher.** Stage.tsx (lesson) and Board.tsx (Talk and drawer) take scene, goto and board commands. Board gains `BoardCard {type:"scene"; scene}`, drawn with SlideView, WidgetView or QuizView under `board.scene.*` spot ids.
- **Recorder: lib/theater/record.ts** (IndexedDB, following the blobs.ts pattern). See the recording section.
- **Replay.** The same player runs over the records. See the recording section.

4. OBSERVATION: lib/theater/observe.ts
`TutorContext` (lib/ai/context.ts:32-45) gains `stage?: {title, kind, state}`. It is built field by field from what is publicly on screen, for example a fraction bar's {parts, shaded, checked}, and never a `target` or answer index (one-workspace §6). The spec's `input` and `spots` fields land in the same change.

5. GENERATOR PATH: background, never inside a turn
- `make_lesson` (an echo-only board tool) hands the client a {title, objective, keyPoints, skillId?} plan, so a one-lesson build skips the outline call.
- The client drives it, as OpenMAIC's use-scene-generator.ts:719-997 does:
  1. POST /api/ai/theater/lesson: writeCourse-style content on model("build"), gateWritten, one retry with reasons, under 60 s.
  2. POST /api/ai/theater/script once per scene, in order, carrying previousSpeeches (the last 150 characters), on model("talk"), under 30 s.
- The first scene can play as soon as its script passes. A closed tab leaves scenes on codeScript, and the scripts resume on the next open.
- Both routes run in this order: model(…, meter) → limited() → Zod → screen() → spendGate("course") → withGenerationRetry (maxRetries 2) → NDJSON.

6. PORTED vs OURS
**Copied with notice:**
- generation-retry.ts (234 lines) → lib/ai/retry.ts, default maxRetries changed from 5 to 2.
- buildCourseContext (prompt-formatters.ts:9-50) → courseContext() with EN/ES strings, plus "you are already talking with this learner; never greet; never say 'last class'".
- Prompt text, minus the "Great job, everyone!" encouragement line, discussion, agents and userProfile:
  - slide-actions/system.md Design Requirements (single voice, same-session continuity, point before you say);
  - quiz-actions answer-safety rules (meta-level only);
  - interactive-actions principles (direct them to touch a named part; start simple);
  - snippets/speech-tts-readability.md.
- The Kaizen delta's TEACHING_DIRECTIVE (lib/kaizen/client/course-request.ts:94-104) → WRITER and the script prompt.
- choreography/cursor.ts and playback/action-navigation.ts, adapted.

**Rewritten as patterns, no code copied:** the PlaybackEngine state machine; first-scene-first with serial scripts; dsl runtime.ts records ordered by a store-assigned seq with anchors that may go stale; op ids for idempotent appends.

**Left behind:** PPTist DSL, renderer and editor; HTML widgets and InteractiveIframeHost; PBL; discussion and agent profiles; Pi and LangGraph directors; StreamBuffer; AudioPlayer; TTS and ASR providers; json-repair; action-parser; every route; lib/ai/*; resolve-model and model-config; the OAuth adapter; Postgres persistence; video export (1.1).

**Ours, unchanged in role:** tutorTurn and tools, Board and cards, Stage, scenes and the 12 typed widgets, writeCourse, gateWritten and gateLesson, the spotlight engine, lib/voice plus the spec's new modules.

New code is about 1,000 lines plus tests: types 60, beat 80, observe 60, script 150, routes and driver 150, player 200, cursor 80, record 150, replay page 150.
design:2.tutorFirst:
Build order follows the owner: the live tutor's voice, anchors and cursor (spec P1–P3) first. The theater sits on top of those exact modules and adds no second sync system.

LIVE SYNC CONTRACT (binding; spec §2.3, §2.5, §3)
1. **One model call per turn.**
   - Director verbs are echo-only BOARD_TOOLS written after the words: `stage_scene`, `go_to_scene`, `make_lesson`, plus the existing show_visual, start_practice, add_to_calendar and note_for_grownup.
   - `stopWhen: [isStepCount(5), last step is board-only]`, so opening a scene costs 0 extra calls.
   - `stage_scene` takes our SceneSchema (schemas.ts): a slide with at most 3 blocks, an interactive with one typed Widget, or a quiz with exactly 1 question.
   - Its execute runs `gateScene` and returns `{shown, problems?}`. gateScene checks: widgetProblems, pictureProblem, praise/filler/emoji/link, languageOf, the K–2 load, that the quiz key resolves, that the hint doesn't name the right choice, and that the starting state isn't already the target.
2. **Anchors.**
   - `[[spot:id]]` goes right before the word it refers to: at most 1 per sentence and 3 per reply.
   - Ids come only from the turn's `spots` list (visibleSpots, at most 60).
   - cueParser holds back at most 80 characters. Markers never reach the bubble, saveThread, notes or the record.
   - point_at and runSpotFromToolPart are deleted (spec §1.3). SpotAgain replays a beat's cues silently.
3. **The voice is the clock.**
   - SpeechOut.speak() returns a SpeechRun with an id. `onWordScheduled(word, audibleAt, run)` feeds the attention scheduler.
   - Timing: arrive at audibleAt − 150 ms. Glide = clamp(240 + 0.3·px, 280, 560) ms on cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1).
   - Dwell: arrivals at least 900 ms apart (K–2: 1200 ms).
   - Limits: at most 5 moves per reply, and at most 1 into an indexed family (tick/cell/part/point/bar) while an item is open.
   - Late cues: up to 300 ms late, shorten the glide; later, crossfade over 150 ms; after the sentence ends, drop.
   - At fire time: the epoch matches, resolveSpot finds it, isShown, and it is not guarded.
   - Browser voices fire on onBoundary. Typed mode fires when the word renders, with the same dwell.
4. **Glow and cursor.**
   - beginPointing({epoch, voice}) runs one persistent ring, tweened by rAF and never re-keyed within a reply, with one pulse per reply.
   - TutorCursor: a 14 px accent dot parked 4 px outside the ring. Its poses follow the state: at the mic while listening; one glide to the learner's bubble while thinking; at home on the newest bubble or the Play button while speaking.
   - Voice mode: no caption and no dim; at most one scroll per reply.
   - Reduced motion: no dot, a 150 ms ring crossfade. Forced colors: the dashed ring.
5. **Epochs and cancelling.**
   - The live epoch is `${pathname}|${item|scene|"talk"}|${messageId}`; the theater epoch is `${pathname}|${scene.id}|${beat.id}`.
   - Barge-in, the learner using any control, or an item, scene or route change cancels pending cues and pending stage commands.
6. **Theater addition.** A scripted `do` command is word-bound like a cue. A live scene or card appears only after the words. A scene put up this turn has no ids in this turn's spots list, so the director prompt says: introduce it in words now, point at its parts next turn.

THE THREE SURFACES
**Talk (/talk).** The board is the stage.
- The latest scene card shows large at the top with `board.scene.*` ids; older cards collapse below.
- Example turn:
  1. "Let's split a bar into fourths."
  2. stage_scene puts up a fraction bar with 4 parts and 0 shaded.
  3. The learner shades parts. The widget's own check() gives the verdict, and the move is recorded.
  4. The next context carries stage.state {parts: 4, shaded: 2, checked: false}.
  5. The tutor says "Look at the [[spot:board.scene.widget.fractionbar.part.1]]second part…".
- For a whole topic, make_lesson shows a "Building: Equivalent fractions" card while the tutor keeps teaching. When the first scene arrives, a "Play it" button appears.

**The drawer beside a problem** (TutorDrawer + Runner).
- The problem itself is the stage. The tutor points at practice.prompt.part.*; the guards (answerSpots plus value parts) hold until it is answered.
- Board cards for worked examples are allowed. stage_scene over the problem is not, because it would cover the work.
- Moving to the next item closes the drawer and cancels speech and cues.

**Lesson stage** (Stage.tsx + TutorPanel).
- The narration bar becomes the performance bar: Play, Pause, Stop and captions. It never starts by itself.
- The player performs each scene's script, using codeScript when a scene has none.
- Tapping Ask or speaking switches to live, a tutorTurn with {surface:"lesson", lesson, scene, spots, stage, heard}.
  - The tutor can point at stage.block.<i>.visual.* and at widget.*, with widget.answer and stage.choice.* guarded until checked.
  - It can go_to_scene to any visited scene, but never past an unanswered check.
- "Back to the lesson" resumes at the cut sentence.
- Script beats on quiz and interactive scenes are meta-only, followed by `wait:"act"`: the check belongs to the learner.

**Today K–2.** The BigHear script from spec §5.5 is one code-built beat.

**Demo mode.** Demo beats with hintSpotAt cues, catalogue lessons on codeScript, and replays all work with no keys.

NUMBERS
- Live turns are unchanged: p50 ≤ 1.6 s from the learner's last word to the first sound for grades 3–9, ≤ 2.4 s for K–2.
- A stage_scene card renders within 100 ms of its tool input completing. That input is streamed after the first sentence, so it adds ≤ 50 ms to first-sound p50.
- Play to first sound: ≤ 400 ms with a warm socket, ≤ 250 ms from a clip.
- Interrupt: tutor ducked within 150 ms and stopped within 800 ms.
- Resume within 300 ms.
design:2.recording:
WHAT A RECORDING IS
**Session header:** `TheaterSession {id, profileId, surface, threadId?, lessonRef?, locale, band, startedAt, status: "live"|"ended", v: 1}`.

**Events:** append-only `TheaterRecord {seq, t, ev}`. `seq` is assigned by the store and is the only order (OpenMAIC's runtime.ts design). `t` is milliseconds since the session started. Each record carries an opId, so a resend is never recorded twice. The `ev` kinds:
- `tutor {beat, run?: {wordsAt: number[] (delta-encoded ms), heardUpTo, cut?}, voice: "vendor"|"device"|"text"}`
- `learner {via: "voice"|"text"|"tap", text}`. The text is scrubbed with scrubFamily at write time, and confidence is kept for voice turns.
- `move {target: SpotId, kind: "select"|"set"|"check", state?: public widget state, verdict?: "right"|"not-yet"}`. The verdict is copied from the code checker.
- `stage {cmd}`
- `safety {kind}` (no text)

**Never stored:** learner audio, raw pointer traces, names, answer keys or prompts.

**Where it lives:** IndexedDB `kaizenedu.theater`, following the blobs.ts pattern. Where IndexedDB is unavailable it falls back to memory, and the UI says "kept for this visit only".

**Sizes:** a tutor beat is about 0.5 KB, a learner turn about 0.1 KB and a move about 0.08 KB, so a 20-minute session is roughly 40–60 KB. Caps are 2,000 records or 512 KB per session, and 200 sessions per learner (matching MAX_THREADS); the oldest unsaved sessions are pruned first.

**Links:** `TutorThread` (planner/types.ts:56) gains `sessionId`, so every transcript can offer "Watch again". lib/export.ts and clearAll cover the database.

**Sync:** in 1.0 recordings stay on the device, and the UI says so. Curated lessons sync through `courses`.

HOW IT REPLAYS
The same player runs over the records, in replay mode:
- tutor beats are spoken again;
- stage commands are applied again;
- learner turns show as captions and are never voiced;
- moves show their recorded state;
- verdicts show muted, as "then: right".

The banner reads "Replay · Tue Oct 6 · doesn't count as practice".

Voice options:
- **With a voice.** The app SpeechOut re-synthesizes in the same voice id (vendor if allowed, otherwise a Tier A device voice). Cues are bound to word indexes, not milliseconds, so they line up with the new clock without any extra work.
- **The original voice.** Only where clips exist (spec P5: catalogue narration and fixed lines, `voice/<sha>.mp3 + .json` with timestamps). Live replies are not stored as audio. 24 kHz PCM is about 48 KB/s, so roughly 58 MB per 20 minutes, and keeping a child's session as audio needs its own consent decision.
- **No voice.** Captions, paced by the recorded wordsAt, with at least 900 ms between moves.

Seeking goes to beat boundaries:
- Stage and board state are rebuilt silently.
- Widget state is restored from the last recorded move snapshot. That needs a controlled `state` prop on the 12 widgets. Until they have it, seeking past a learner move replays from the start, and the UI says so.

Replay writes no Attempt, ActivityEvent or TeachingAct. "Try it yourself" starts a new live session.

HOW A RECORDING BECOMES A LESSON
"Keep this as a lesson" runs `curateSession(records)`:
1. The scenes are those that were on stage: stage_scene scenes plus lesson scenes.
2. Each scene's script is the tutor beats said while it was showing. Their cues are checked again against that scene's spot list.
3. Learner turns are dropped. Learner moves become `wait:"act"` points. Verdicts are dropped.
4. gateScript, gateLesson and gateWritten run on the result.

The lesson needs at least one check scene; otherwise the session can only be kept as notes. It is saved as a Course with origin "generated" and `ai: true` when any beat is AI, plus `from: {sessionId, date}`. It is family-only and never written to the shared server course cache.

HOW LESSONS MULTIPLY
1. **Tutor-made:** make_lesson runs the generator in the background.
2. **Curated** from sessions.
3. **"Make another like this":** the same objectives and keyPoints with new numbers, examples and interests (seeded). It is linked to the original, passes the same gates, and the original is kept.
4. **Catalogue seeds:** the 48 courses get codeScript at build time with no AI, and they play in the theater on day one. Authored cues and clips come later; the courses get fixed, not extended.
5. **Generic AI lessons** are cached per (goal, grade, locale), as writeCourse already does, so the next family gets one instantly.
6. **Thumbs up or down** on every theater lesson (the owner asked for this on 2026-10-03). A thumbs-down offers "Make it again".
design:2.honesty:
LABELS
- Every beat carries `by`, and the UI shows it: "AI tutor" or "Demo tutor" (said once), and "Using this device's voice" whenever the voice isn't the vendor voice.
- Lessons say where they came from: "Written by people", "Built from real sources", "Written by AI", or "From your session · <date>".
- Replays carry the banner "Replay · <date> · doesn't count as practice".
- AI is never claimed for code-built scripts.

PRACTICE IS NOT PROOF
- The theater changes no mastery rule; learning/engine.ts RULES are untouched.
- Lesson checks stay activity.
- **When something counts as help:**
  - the tutor panel open beside a check (the existing Stage.tutorHelps);
  - any live turn on a check scene;
  - a scripted demonstration, which is only allowed on show scenes and never on the widget being answered.
- **What stays neutral:** script beats on check scenes. They are meta-only, enforced by gateScript with the quiz answer-safety rules plus `mentions()` against the choice text.
- Replays and curated lessons never count as practice.

ANSWERS ARE CHECKED BY CODE
- Verdicts come only from a widget's check(), the quiz answer index or the practice checker. A move record copies that verdict.
- Generated quiz keys must resolve (gateLesson). OpenMAIC short_answer and model grading are never imported.
- The stage observation sent to the tutor is built field by field, and no target or answer index ever reaches a prompt.
- writeScript sees the prompts and choices, never the key.
- Cue targets go through three layers:
  1. `z.enum(pointableSpots(scene))` at decode, which excludes guarded ids;
  2. guardSpots at fire time;
  3. a test that runs every catalogue and generated scene's cues against answerSpots, widget.answer and stage.choice.*.
- No counting along.

DEMO MODE
The whole theater runs with no keys:
- demo beats with hintSpotAt cues;
- catalogue lessons on codeScript;
- replays in typed or device-voice mode.

make_lesson in demo mode builds a source-built course (lib/source-course.ts) with codeScript, labelled as such.

SAFETY
- screen() runs before every model call:
  - tutorTurn already does;
  - /api/ai/course does not today (route.ts:29-48), so it is added in T0;
  - /api/ai/theater/lesson and /script screen the goal and any text the client sends.
- Generated text passes gateWritten (praise, filler, emoji, links, language) and suitable() before a child sees or hears it.
- Fixed referrals stay as they are. Safety records keep the kind only, never the text.

PRIVACY
- **Names:** learner names never go to a model. scrubContext and scrubMessages handle the tutor request, and aiFetch must be used everywhere: lib/generate.ts:104 still uses plain fetch, which T0 fixes.
- **OpenMAIC identity fields:** userNickname, userBio and userProfile are never ported; we take no code path that has them.
- **Recordings:** scrubbed when written. No microphone audio, ever.
- **Replay voice:** replays re-speak only the tutor's words, under the same consent rule as live speech: under 13, vendor TTS needs a grown-up's consent until counsel rules.
- **Storage:** recordings stay on the device. Export and delete cover them.

THE OAUTH ADAPTER NEVER SHIPS
- `npm run verify` greps apps/ for `sk-ant-oat|claude-code-20250219|oauth-2025-04-20|You are Claude Code|anthropic-oauth|startAnthropicOAuthRefresh` and fails on a hit.
- An ESLint no-restricted-imports rule bans `modules/` and any `@openmaic/*` import.
- No route, lib/ai, resolve-model, model-config or instrumentation file from OpenMAIC is copied.

LICENCE
OpenMAIC is MIT, © 2026 THU-MAIC. The notice goes in a header on each copied file and in apps/web/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, which lists every source path.

risks: Latency. A generator call inside a turn would break the 1.6 s budget: OpenMAIC's own historical run took more than 8 minutes per scene at max effort. Mitigation: live beats come from the one tutor call; director verbs are echo-only tools after the words; lessons are generated in the background, driven by the client, with requests under 60 s; the T4 eval checks that first-sound p50 changes by no more than 50 ms.

A scene put up this turn can't be pointed at in the same reply: its ids aren't in the turn's spots list, and the tool input arrives after the speech has started. This is accepted by design; the prompt introduces the scene in words and points at it next turn. If dogfooding finds this stilted, the fix is to show the card the moment its tool input arrives, never a second model call.

The 12 widgets keep their state inside React (e.g. FractionBar's useState). Replay seek, curated `wait:act` points and scripted demonstrations all need controlled state props. Until then, seeking past a learner move replays from the start, and the UI says so honestly.

The narration model differs. OpenMAIC writes speech that differs from the words on the slide, while K–2 read-along needs the words highlighted on screen. Beats with `read` must equal the segment text (validated), and every other beat shows as a caption. Without this, K–2 lessons lose read-along.

The tutor could point at an answer, or set up a scene that is already solved. The defences are z.enum over pointable spots at decode, guardSpots at fire time, gateScene's 'starting state is not the target' rule, quiz answer-safety for script beats, and a test over every catalogue and generated scene. A gap in any one of these is an honesty bug, not a style issue.

Help accounting. A live turn on a check scene and a scripted demonstration on a widget must mark help; script beats on check scenes must stay neutral. The rule changes no mastery number, but if it is implemented wrong, help on an answer goes unrecorded.

Storage. IndexedDB can be evicted (Safari can drop data from sites not used for a while) or blocked in private windows. Recordings are best-effort device data and the UI says so. Only curated lessons go to the synced store. A long session could pass 512 KB, which the caps and pruning must handle.

Prompt heritage. OpenMAIC's slide-actions prompt asks for encouragement in speech ('Great job, everyone!'), greets on the first page, and assumes multiple agents with discussion. Remove these when porting the text. The PRAISE gate and the 'already talking, never greet' context catch anything left over. The fallback narration in its source is hard-coded Chinese, so our fallback is codeScript in the learner's locale.

Layered retries and cost. withGenerationRetry (2), the gate retry (1) and the per-scene script calls stack up: up to 6 calls for content plus 3 per script. Every attempt goes through meter() and spendGate. stage_scene adds about 300 output tokens to a turn. The spend caps stay the backstop.

Vercel limits. A client-driven, resumable job keeps each request under 60 s, but closing a tab stops generation. Scenes fall back to codeScript and their scripts resume on the next open, so nothing broken ships.

A stale merge. worktree-wf_a6840288 predates the content merge; merged as a branch, its diff deletes about 127k lines of content. Its work is already on foundation as 3d3d518 and its neighbours. Agents must not re-merge it, and the maps' 'blocked on 5cffe4c' must not stall T1.

Live Tutor P0 is blocked on keys (ElevenLabs, Deepgram). The theater is built against fakes, so real-voice word drift (≤ 1 word at 60) and replay re-sync stay unproven until the keys arrive. They must be reported as blocked, not done.

Replay audio and consent. Re-speaking tutor text with the vendor voice sends it to ElevenLabs again. That needs the same under-13 consent as live speech. Storing a live session's audio would need a new consent decision and about 58 MB per 20 minutes, so it is out.

Model-written facts. Generated widget configs and slide text are structure-checked, but a fact (a moon phase, a science claim) is still the model's word. The 'Written by AI' label, gateWritten and suitable() limit this; teacher review stays the bar for the catalogue.

OAuth and licence. Copying any OpenMAIC route, lib/ai file, resolve-model or model-config pulls in providers.ts and its OAuth branch through static imports. Port only the listed leaf files, with the verify grep and the ESLint ban as guards. Keep the THU-MAIC MIT notice; never copy the PPTist-derived slide model (its provenance is unclear) or mathml2omml (LGPL).

design:0.name: KaizenEDU Tutor Theater: OpenMAIC's engine behind our stage, one Beat for live, recorded and replayed
design:0.tutorFirst:
PRECONDITION: the tutor branch appears to have landed already
- 5cffe4c is not an ancestor of foundation. But `git cherry foundation 5cffe4c` lists 17 of its 19 patches as present.
- Its last fix is on foundation as 3d3d518, with the same subject.
- The two patches marked "+" (28e9c87 Talk with board, 36ef28b) landed reworked: 9dd173f has 36ef28b's subject, and Board.tsx and cards.ts exist on foundation. Later fixes build on them (7bd494c, 8d71411).
- So spec §0.4 and the code map's "blocked" note look stale. Confirm by diffing TutorChat.tsx, update the spec, and never fork TutorChat. The recorder subscribes from outside it, through replyText().

ORDER
1. Live tutor P1–P3 as the spec writes it. Nothing in the theater ships before the app SpeechOut, cues.ts, attention.ts and the pointing session exist.
2. Every surface below then uses one engine instance per mount. All of them share the VoiceRoot SpeechOut, one AudioContext and the single pointing store.

THE SYNC CONTRACT (binding, from spec §3, the same for live and replayed Beats)
- **Anchors replace point_at.**
  - The model writes `[[spot:id]]` right before the word it names. The marker is held back until `]]`, for at most 80 chars.
  - cue.word is the index of the first word after the marker. A marker at the very end binds to the last word.
  - Ids must come from the `spots` list sent with that turn. `point_at` and runSpotFromToolPart are deleted: each point cost a tool step, about 0.6–1.2 s of silence, and was timed by the text stream rather than the voice.
- **The voice is the clock.** player.ts emits onWordScheduled(word, audibleAt, run), where audibleAt includes outputLatency.
- **Timing:**
  - The cursor arrives 150 ms before the word.
  - Glide = clamp(240 + 0.3·px, 280, 560) ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1).
  - Arrivals are ≥ 900 ms apart (1200 ms for K–2). A cue later than 300 ms past its word is dropped.
  - At most 5 moves per reply, and at most 1 per scripted beat or 3 per beat-sentence group.
  - No counting along: at most 1 move per reply into any `*.tick.*`, `*.cell.*` or `*.part.<i>` family while an item is open.
- **Fire-time checks:** epoch match, resolveSpot, isShown, guardSpots. Retry every 100 ms until the sentence ends, then drop silently.
- **Epoch** = `${pathname}|${item.id | scene.id | 'talk'}|${messageId}`. For scripted beats the last part is `script:${takeId}:${beatId}`.
- **Look:**
  - One persistent ring, tweened with rAF and never re-keyed. One pulse per reply.
  - A 14 px accent TutorCursor dot that parks 4 px outside the ring.
  - Voice mode: no dim and no caption.
  - Reduced motion: a 150 ms crossfade and no dot.
  - Forced colors: the dashed Highlight ring.
- **Browser voices:** cues fire on onBoundary with a 200 ms glide. A voice with no word boundaries fires at sentence start.
- **Typed mode:** audibleAt is the moment the word renders.
- **Cancel all pending cues on:** barge-in, speech cancel, any learner pointerdown/keydown on a control, item/scene/route change, or epoch change.
- **Latency stays the spec's:**
  - last word → first sound: p50 ≤ 1.6 s (3–9), ≤ 2.4 s (K–2);
  - acknowledgement ≤ 150 ms;
  - duck ≤ 150 ms; stop ≤ 800 ms.
  - The theater adds zero work to the turn path: recording writes to IndexedDB after `finish`, and lesson generation is a separate request.

TALK (app/(focus)/talk, TutorChat + Board)
- Each reply is a live take: tutorTurn (safety screen → spoken precheck → ONE streamText with the cached static prompt; stopWhen stops after a board-only step) → useChat parts → liveBeats() → engine.live(beats).
- Board tools (show_visual, start_practice, add_to_calendar, note_for_grownup, and the new make_lesson) are echo-only and come after the words. They become `do: board` Beats.
- `spots` = the visibleSpots() ids. The latest show_visual card carries `board.visual.*` ids so K–2 picture-first turns can point at parts of the picture.
- "Show me again" (SpotAgain) replays the message's recorded cues with dwell spacing and no audio.

DRAWER BESIDE A PROBLEM (TutorDrawer + Runner)
- The same live path.
- Guards: answerSpots(item) plus the value families (visual.clock.number.*, visual.numberline.tick.*, visual.tenframe.cell.*, visual.coord.point.*, visual.linegraph.point.*, visual.bargraph.bar.*).
- A spoken answer is checked in code on the server before the model call; the model is told the verdict.
- Item change (Next) closes the drawer and cancels speech and cues.
- The take is referenced to the practice set id.

LESSON STAGE (Stage.tsx: the tutor performs, then goes live on the same stage)
- **Play** runs the scene's script through the engine. With no AI it is codeScript: it reads the on-screen words, keeps the "say it with me" turn gaps, and puts the auto cue on each picture.
- **Interrupting:** the learner speaks (duck within 150 ms; cancel on a real word or after 700 ms of voiced frames), types in the panel, or touches a widget. Then engine.interrupt() saves {scene, beat, sentence} and the mode becomes live.
- **The live turn's TutorContext:**
  - lesson {title, the scene's words: never quiz keys};
  - spots = sceneSpots(scene), pointable only;
  - `said`: the heard prefix of the current beat (heardUpTo + ' [interrupted]', per spec §2.4 truncation) and the previous beat's last 150 chars (OpenMAIC's previousSpeeches idea).
  - With that, the reply continues the thread and points at the same stage ids.
- **Resuming:** "go on", the Continue chip, or for K–2 a 56 px "Keep going" chip resumes at the cut sentence. Nothing auto-resumes.
- **Handoff beats** end the show part of try/check scenes and switch to yourTurn:
  - the widget or choices belong to the learner;
  - the mic follows the conversation-mode rules;
  - checking is code (widget check(), QuizView);
  - after the check the tutor reacts live, or in demo mode with the code-built `explain` line.
- **Touching a widget during a pose beat** cancels the pose. The widget becomes the learner's at its current state: "show, let them touch it, then check".
- **Phones:** the panel sheet peeks to ≤ 35dvh at the first move (spec §3.4).

THE TUTOR MAKES LESSONS (the owner's "it will create more and more")
- The new echo-only board tool `make_lesson {goal ≤ 200 chars, subject, grade}` shows a "Making a lesson on …" card.
- The browser then runs the generation flow. The tutor keeps teaching live in the conversation meanwhile, with no filler speech.
- When scene 1 has content and a script, the card turns to "Ready, play it here".
- The tutor proposes make_lesson only when the learner asks to learn something, or when the same skill was stuck in 2+ sittings (learning/profile).
- Cap: 3 per learner per day (KAIZEN_LESSONS_PER_DAY), plus the spend caps.
design:0.honesty:
LABELS (one line each, always visible on the TheaterBar/ReplayFrame)
- "Live" or "Replay · <date>" in a distinct frame.
- Origin of the words: "Lesson by people · narration read from the page" (codeScript); "Narration written by AI" (an AI script over a catalogue lesson); "Written by AI" (a generated lesson); "Built from real sources"; "Demo tutor", said once in the opening.
- A fallback says so: "This scene is read from the page".
- A kept variant says "Explained live on <date>".

PRACTICE IS NOT PROOF
- Replay mode writes nothing: no Attempt, ActivityEvent, TeachingAct, review or thread.
  - Enforced by a store-diff test, and by the replay engine having no recorder or acts import (a lint boundary).
- Watching a scripted lesson is exposure, not help:
  - neutral narration and navigation never mark a check assisted (the one-workspace §5 "tutor present ≠ tutor helped" rule);
  - the live tutor opened on a scene keeps today's rule: every check on that scene counts as helped;
  - quiz scripts may only frame the activity, and gateScript makes that true.
- Lesson checks stay practice-only, and the mastery law in learning/engine.ts is unchanged.

ANSWERS CHECKED BY CODE
- Scripts and live replies never decide right or wrong. Quiz scenes use QuizView with index keys, widgets use their check(), practice uses check(). No model ever grades (OpenMAIC's quiz-grade, its short_answer and its iframe widgets are not ported).
- gateScript rejects:
  - a quiz beat that mentions any choice text or the explain text (mentions() as in the hint gate), or that teaches the concept: ≤ 2 beats and anchors only on stage.quiz.prompt;
  - an anchor on a guarded or unlisted id;
  - a pose equal to, or within one step of, the widget's target, or out of range (poseProblems, beside widgetProblems);
  - a pose for sorter, sequence or sentence-builder;
  - more than one handoff, or a handoff anywhere but the end of a try/check scene.
- Fire-time guards run again in the browser.
- The tutor prompt never contains a key: items are rebuilt server-side, and the scene text has no answers.

DEMO MODE (KAIZEN_AI=off, no keys)
- Everything plays: codeScript for every lesson, demo-tutor replies as Beats with hintSpotAt cues, browser Tier A/B voices or clips, and replays from IndexedDB offline.
- make_lesson is offered only with a provider. Without one, the tutor offers the source-built course path (lib/source-course.ts).

SAFETY
- screen() runs before every model call:
  - /api/ai/course does not do this today (route.ts has no screen()); fix it first;
  - /api/ai/lesson screens the goal;
  - tutorTurn already screens every turn.
- /api/ai/script inputs are model-written scene content that already passed suitable(); scripts pass suitable() and gateScript.
- No generated JavaScript, no iframes, no third-party CDNs or fonts (never import renderer/fonts.css).
- Ported prompts drop the line "Encouragements … (e.g., 'Great job, everyone!')" (slide-actions/system.md), which breaks our PRAISE rule; praiseIn() runs on every script.
- The fallback narration is ours and locale-correct. OpenMAIC's hard-coded Chinese defaults (scene-generator.ts:1863-2028) never ship.

PRIVACY
- Learner names never go to a model:
  - scripts receive scene content, band, locale and spot labels only;
  - never userNickname, userBio or userProfile (outline-generator.ts:89-92, scene-generator.ts:1738);
  - lib/generate.ts must post through aiFetch, not plain fetch (lib/generate.ts:104), so goals are scrubbed;
  - spot labels go through setSpotScrub.
- Takes hold learner text scrubbed by withoutNames at write time, and never mic audio. Bodies stay on the device in IndexedDB until sync; they are in family export and delete.
- Private clips use allocated ids. Content-addressed clips are only for public text.
- OAuth: a CI check (scripts/check-forbidden.ts in npm run verify) fails on sk-ant-oat, claude-code-20250219, oauth-2025-04-20, anthropic-oauth, startAnthropicOAuthRefresh and the "You are Claude Code" string anywhere in apps/web.
- MIT: a THU-MAIC notice on every copied file plus THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

risks: Latency. A generated scene is two sequential model calls. The historical run at max effort took more than 8 minutes per scene (docs/history/.../openmaic.yml:42-45), so generation can never sit inside a live turn (p50 1.6 s). It runs as a background, browser-driven job, and the tutor keeps teaching live meanwhile. If p50 to first beat goes over 45 s, lower the build effort for scripts before cutting quality gates.

Vercel duration. /api/ai/course has maxDuration 300, and a full 8-lesson course on Opus can exceed it. The new path splits the work into ≤ 120 s content requests and ≤ 30 s script requests that the browser drives, which also gives resume. The old writeCourse 'full' path needs the same split.

K–2 read-along versus a script. OpenMAIC speech is deliberately not the on-screen words ('slides show, speech tells'), while K–2 needs the read-aloud word highlight of the words on screen. For K–2 slides, codeScript stays the reading. AI beats are allowed only as transitions and 'your turn' lines, or else shown as a caption with the word highlight.

Uncontrolled widgets. All 12 widgets keep internal useState, so poses and seek need a controlled `pose` prop. Risks are regressions in widgets.test.tsx and seek being disabled after the first manipulation. Keep pose pre-touch only, and record learner poses as semantic state for seek.

Storage. The store is a single localStorage JSON document (about 5 MB quota), so take bodies must go to IndexedDB. Safari can evict script-written storage after 7 days without interaction, so takes may vanish on iOS until server sync covers them. Say plainly 'Replays are kept on this device' until sync lands.

Two sync formats competing. If anyone ports OpenMAIC's interleaved text/action JSON alongside spec §3.1 anchors, live and recorded sessions drift apart. Rule: anchors are the only text syntax and Beat is the only stored form. action-parser.ts and json-repair.ts are never ported; json-repair also corrupts single-backslash LaTeX (\frac parses as a form feed).
